data.title: Malware found in official gravityforms plugin indicating supply chain breach
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 文章报道了GravityForms插件官方版本中发现恶意软件，表明存在供应链 breach。最初在7月10日发现问题，恶意代码通过HTTP请求连接到可疑的gravityapi.org域名。技术分析显示，恶意代码收集网站信息并发送至该域名。GravityForms在版本2.9.12中包含后门，但随后迅速移除。7月11日，发布2.9.13版本修复问题，Namecheap也暂停了相关域名。监控显示感染范围不大，仅影响手动下载和composer安装。Patchstack团队正在调查，并提醒用户检查是否受影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gravity Forms安全事件的细节、影响范围及可能原因

不同观点：
• neomantra认为，此次安全 breach 能够被发现，得益于系统操作员的 diligent tracking，类似于之前xz breach通过开发者发现异常性能回归而被揭露。这表明细致的监控对发现安全问题至关重要。
• anthonyeden引用了Gravity Forms的官方声明，指出只有通过直接下载或Composer安装的用户会受到影响，并关注到官方尚未提及是否会聘请第三方安全公司调查此事。
• rectang转述了RocketGenius工作人员的确认，即恶意软件只影响手动下载和通过Composer安装的插件，对此表示松了一口气。
• mpol指出，如果在检查表单之前使用nonce，可以防止许多问题，暗示这能减少手动工作量，强调技术措施在防范中的作用。
• doodlebugging对文章中的日期错误表示关注，认为这是编辑上的失误，虽然不影响事件本身，但可能影响读者理解。
• hammyhavoc质疑此次安全问题未被及时发现的时间长度，表明对响应速度的担忧。
• bhk关注此次事件的影响范围，询问是广泛影响互联网上的大量网站，还是仅限于少数低流量网站。
• mmsc仅简短提及了Ac1dB1tch3z，没有深入讨论。
• giingyui认为应明确指出涉及的插件名称，以增加透明度。
• kristianc批评了Gravity Forms的高价扩展，质疑这是否反映了WordPress生态系统的问题，包括其安全性、开发者可能的欺诈行为以及非技术用户的易受骗性。
• iambateman对事件的可能性质提出疑问，怀疑是否是GravityForms内部人员所为，并指出文章中未明确说明此事。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是事件的发现和透明度，部分评论（如neomantra和anthonyeden）关注发现过程及官方回应的充分性。
• 另一个讨论点是事件的技术细节，如mpol对nonce使用的建议，表明如何通过技术手段防止类似问题。
• 事件的影响范围和可能的原因也是讨论的重点，bhk和iambateman对此提出了具体的疑问和猜测。
• 最后，kristianc对WordPress生态系统的广泛批评引发对高价插件和用户安全的思考。

Published 11 July 2025
Rafie Muhammad
Lead Security Researcher at Patchstack
Supply Chain Attack
Security Advisories

Update 8-11-2025 06:00 UTC:
We have observed some activity in regard to one of the backdoors that involves a gf_api_token parameter. The IP address 193.160.101.6 tries to request, for every site, the following URLs with a spoofed user agent:
/wp-content/plugins/gravityforms_2.9.12/notification.php?gf_api_token=Cx3VGSwAHkB9yzIL9Qi48IFHwKm4sQ6Te5odNtBYu6Asb9JX06KYAWmrfPtG1eP3&action=ping
/wp-content/plugins/gravityforms_2.9.11.1/notification.php?gf_api_token=Cx3VGSwAHkB9yzIL9Qi48IFHwKm4sQ6Te5odNtBYu6Asb9JX06KYAWmrfPtG1eP3&action=ping
/wp-content/plugins/gravityforms/notification.php?gf_api_token=Cx3VGSwAHkB9yzIL9Qi48IFHwKm4sQ6Te5odNtBYu6Asb9JX06KYAWmrfPtG1eP3&action=ping
Update 7-11-2025 14:10 UTC
: A version
2.9.13
has been released to ensure customers can safely update to a new version without a backdoor present. In addition, Namecheap (the domain registrar) has suspended the domain name gravityapi.org to avoid successful exploitation of the backdoor portion that connects to this domain name.
Update 7-11-2025 12:38 UTC
: We received from our reporter both the copy of the vulnerable version and the patched version of the plugin. Technical details are updated in this article. We also received a confirmation from one of the staff of RocketGenius that the malware only affects manual downloads and composer installation of the plugin.
Update 7-11-2025 12:07 UTC
: We received information from our reporter that GravityForm responded to his initial email and confirmed that they are doing an investigation for a malware breach on their product. The reporter claims that the initial malicious code was found in version
2.9.12
(which is the latest version of the plugin currently); however, the malicious code itself has now been removed from the code when users try to re-download the package. We also updated more IOCs in this article.
Update 7-11-2025 12:00 UTC
: We've been in touch with multiple large web hosting companies who have scanned their servers for the IOCs. The infection does not seem to be widespread, which could mean that the backdoored plugin was only available for a very short period of time and only delivered to a small number of users.

Patchstack team

here

gravityforms.com

gravityapi.org

data.title: Incus – Next-generation system container, application container, and VM manager
data.author: motorest
data.article_summary: Incus 是一个下一代系统容器、应用容器和虚拟机管理工具，提供类似公有云的用户体验，支持容器和虚拟机混合使用，共享存储和网络资源。它基于镜像，支持多种Linux发行版，具备灵活性和可扩展性，适用于不同场景。Incus可通过命令行工具、REST API或第三方工具管理实例，并提供单一API用于本地和远程访问。它由社区驱动，作为Canonical的LXD的替代方案，由原LXD团队主导开发。Incus支持多种存储后端和网络类型，适用于从单机到大规模集群的部署，并提供备份、快照和实例迁移等功能。Incus适用于任何近期Linux发行版，客户端也可在Windows和macOS上使用。Incus有LTS和功能版本发布，并提供商业支持。项目采用Apache 2许可证，源码托管于GitHub。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Incus工具的特性、使用场景及其与其它工具（如Proxmox、Docker、K8s等）的比较

不同观点：
• **Incus作为Proxmox的替代品**：Semaphor认为Incus是一个Proxmox的替代方案，主要卖点是完全开源且没有企业版。链接中提到了一些切换到Incus的理由。
• **Incus在开发中的优势**：danofsteel32指出Incus在开发Ansible playbooks时非常有用，相比Docker/Podman，其优势在于systemd开箱即用。
• **网站问题**：mathfailure提到Incus的官网无法打开，认为这是一个不好的信号。
• **简便的VM配置**：tcfhgj认为Incus是唯一一个无需GUI就能轻松配置VM的工具。
• **与Docker的区别**：actinium226在学习教程后，仍不清楚Incus与Docker的区别。

补充讨论：
• **使用场景**：gavinray询问Incus的使用场景，询问其与K8s或Fargate/Cloudrun等无服务器容器运行时的区别，以及是否适用于自建云服务或管理组织内部的VM基础设施。
• **与Colima的集成**：mdaniel提到通过Colima支持Incus，并提供了相关链接。
• **系统更新和内核升级问题**：63stack担心在运行Incus的机器上进行系统更新时可能导致的VM/容器崩溃问题，并询问如何处理内核升级需要重启的情况。
• **兼容性**：manosyja询问Incus可以与哪些技术配合使用，猜测可能是LXCs和QEMU VMs。
• **高级功能**：sigmonsays指出Incus的不同存储后端及其功能是值得注意的特性，特别是btrfs、lvm和zfs的快照和精简配置支持。
• **资源隔离与多租户支持**：burnt-resistor认为Incus在资源隔离、限制、优先级和多租户支持方面不如Type 1 hypervisor，这对大规模运行至关重要。
• **LXC用户是否应迁移到Incus**：pm2222询问LXC用户是否应迁移到Incus。
• **名称混淆**：Lightkey提醒不要将Incus与cirrus7的同名产品混淆，并提供了相关链接。
• **Terraform/Pulumi集成**：oulipo询问是否有Terraform或Pulumi集成，以便更容易地部署到运行Incus的VM上。

争议焦点：
• **Incus的定位和使用场景**：用户对Incus的具体使用场景和其与Docker、K8s等工具的区别存在疑问，特别是其是否适合大规模或多租户环境。
• **系统更新和资源管理**：用户对如何安全地进行系统更新以及Incus在资源隔离和管理方面的能力表示关注。

44539338.article_content:
Incus
Introduction
Go to Table of Contents
What is Incus?
¶
Incus is a next-generation system container, application container, and virtual machine manager.
It provides a user experience similar to that of a public cloud. With it, you can easily mix and match both containers and virtual machines, sharing the same underlying storage and network.
Incus is image based and provides images for a
wide number of Linux distributions
. It provides flexibility and scalability for various use cases, with support for different storage backends and network types and the option to install on hardware ranging from an individual laptop or cloud instance to a full server rack.
When using Incus, you can manage your instances (containers and VMs) with a simple command line tool, directly through the REST API or by using third-party tools and integrations. Incus implements a single REST API for both local and remote access.
The Incus project
was created
by Aleksa Sarai as a community driven alternative to Canonical's LXD.
Today, it's led and maintained by many of the same people that once created LXD.
Get started
¶
To get a better idea of what Incus is and what it does, you can
try it online
!
Then if you want to run it locally, take a look at our
getting started guide
.
Containers and virtual machines
¶
Incus provides support for system containers, application containers, and virtual machines.
When running a system container, Incus simulates a virtual version of a full operating system. To do this, it uses the functionality provided by the kernel running on the host system.
When running an application container, Incus runs isolated applications within the host's operating system using container images, similar to how Docker operates.
When running a virtual machine, Incus uses the hardware of the host system, but the kernel is provided by the virtual machine. Therefore, virtual machines can be used to run, for example, a different operating system.
You can learn more about the differences between application containers, system containers and virtual machines in
our documentation
.
Features
¶
Some of the biggest features of Incus are:
Core API
Secure by design
(through unprivileged containers, resource restrictions, authentication, ...)
Intuitive
(with a simple, clear API and crisp command line experience)
Scalable
(from containers on your laptop to clusters of thousands of compute nodes)
Event based
(providing logging, operation, and lifecycle events)
Remote usage
(same API used for local and network access)
Project support
(as a way to compartmentalize sets of images and profiles)
Instances and profiles
Image based
(with images for a wide variety of Linux distributions, published daily)
Instances
(containers and virtual-machines)
Configurable through profiles
(applicable to both containers and virtual machines)
Backup and export
Backup and recovery
(for all objects managed by Incus)
Snapshots
(to save and restore the state of an instance)
Container and image transfer
(between different hosts, using images)
Instance migration
(importing existing instances or transferring them between servers)
Configurability
Multiple storage backends
(with configurable storage pools and storage volumes)
Network management
(including bridge creation and configuration, cross-host tunnels, ...)
Advanced resource control
(CPU, memory, network I/O, block I/O, disk usage and kernel resources)
Device passthrough
(USB, GPU, unix character and block devices, NICs, disks and paths)
Availability
¶
Incus works on any recent Linux distribution.
Incus upstream doesn't directly provide packages, but packages are available in a number of distributions or can be found in 3rd party repositories.
In addition, the Incus client is available for Windows and macOS. You can use the client to connect to an Incus server running on a Linux machine.
Current installation instructions can be found in our
installation guide
.
Support
¶
Incus has two kind of releases:
LTS releases
Feature releases
The current LTS release is Incus 6.0 and is supported until June 2029.
Feature releases are pushed out every month or so and contain new features as well as bugfixes.
The normal support length for those releases is of about a month, or until the next release comes out.
Some Linux distributions might offer longer support for particular feature releases that they decided to ship.
Commercial support for Incus can be obtained from
Zabbly
.
Language, licensing and contributions
¶
Incus is written in Go. It is free software and developed under the
Apache 2 license
.
The Incus source code is available on
GitHub
.
There are no CLA or similar legal agreements required to contribute to Incus. However, we require commits be signed-off (following the DCO - Developer Certificate of Ownership). See the
Contribution guidelines
for more information.

主要讨论点：政府预算和全球卫星跟踪项目的资金分配与责任归属

不同观点：
• **支持项目并强调其价值**：[tomrod] 认为减少政府开支是可以理解的，但这类项目具有高价值，每一块钱的投入都会产生显著的直接和间接效益。他主张回归合理的预算评估原则。

• **国际合作与联合国角色**：[stego-tech] 建议将此类项目交给联合国而非个别国家或私人公司，以确保全球需求获得全球支持，避免一个国家的失败影响全球。但同时也指出，由于安理会成员的利益，这种合作目前不太可能实现。

• **重新分配资金**：[wnevets] 提出撤销对ICE的资助，用以防止卫星相撞，表明其对现有资金分配的不满。

• **责任归属与私营企业参与**：[ThinkBeat] 认为应由拥有卫星和太空 debris 的国家和公司出资，并质疑某些国家是否希望隐藏其间谍卫星的轨迹。

• **免费数据和开放平台**：[JackMorgan] 介绍了自己创建的免费平台，提供空间天气和卫星数据，强调数据免费开放的重要性，并计划推出更多历史数据。

• **反对意见和讽刺**：[sitzkrieg] 对安全措施和科技行业持讽刺态度，暗示对某些技术解决方案的不满。

• **担忧和风险**：[more_corn] 表达了对潜在重大碰撞引发连锁效应的担忧。

• **自由市场的角色**：[ccorcos] 质疑为何自由市场未能承担这一任务，认为已有足够激励让其他方参与其中。

• **简化讨论**：[JSR_FDED] 认为无需过度思考，长期项目最终都会失败。

• **质疑项目合理性**：[TylerJaacks] 希望听到支持该项目的好理由，表明其对项目合理性的质疑。

• **政治和阴谋论**：[ourmandave] 提到气候变化研究卫星被破坏的可能性，并引用"Sharpie Gate"事件，暗示政治干预和金钱利益的关联。

• **预算现实**：[djoldman] 指出即使削减所有非核心项目，美国联邦政府的赤字仍然巨大，暗示削减科学等领域开支并非解决赤字问题的关键。

补充讨论：
• **简短评论**：[Ylpertnodi] 表达了对讨论的冷静态度，[water9] 认为只有大家同意且NOAA不主导时，项目才能成功，[hdb385] 仅表示不满。

争议焦点：
• **资金来源与责任分配**：各方对是否应由政府、私营企业或国际组织出资和管理存在分歧。
• **项目价值与必要性**：部分评论者质疑项目的合理性和必要性，而另一些人则强调其重要性和潜在效益。
• **政治因素**：讨论中涉及政治干预和阴谋论，反映了对政府和国际组织的不信任。

data.title: Context Engineering Guide
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
**总结：**

"上下文工程"（Context Engineering）是“提示工程”（Prompt Engineering）的演进，现被重新定义为优化大型语言模型（LLM）任务执行所需指令和上下文的过程。它不仅涉及简单的提示，还包括设计和管理提示链、调整指令、搜索和准备相关知识、增强查询、工具定义、优化少样本示例、结构化输入输出等。其核心是优化提供给LLM的信息，去除噪音信息，并通过正式的评估流程（如eval pipelines）衡量效果。作者通过一个多代理深度研究应用的具体例子展示了上下文工程的实际操作，如设计系统提示、管理搜索计划代理等，强调了上下文工程在AI代理工作流开发中的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“工程”一词在软件及AI领域中的使用及其合理性的争论

不同观点：
• 一些人认为将某些工作称为“工程”是不准确的，因为这些工作缺乏传统工程所需的严格流程控制、系统化文档和规范等。例如，[zmmmmm] 指出，许多人只想用“工程”这个词来显得高大上，但并不遵循工程的严谨标准，最终还是需要真正的工程师来收拾残局。
• [Sebastian_09] 表示，“提示工程”和“上下文工程”只是面对模型随机性时的次优选择，真正需要的是科学上的进步，而不是更多的“LinkedIn AI网红”传播这些概念。
• [spicyusername] 支持不滥用“工程”一词，认为当前的领域和真正的工程相去甚远，使用这个词汇显得尴尬。

补充讨论：
• [thorum] 提出，上下文工程的真正挑战在于如何从系统中收集LLM完成任务所需的信息，比如GitHub Copilot如何决定展示哪些代码片段，这比简单的提示工程要复杂得多，且提示工程的重要性会随着模型改进而减弱。
• [_Algernon_] 用讽刺的口吻将当前的一些做法比作炼金术，暗示其缺乏科学性和可靠性。
• [xnx] 认为，如果无法证明复杂方法比简单方法更有效，那么这些做法可能只是迷信。
• [adidoit] 关注到“上下文工程”这一新词可能推动“生成式AI认证行业”的发展。
• [gavinh] 表达了对这些讨论的疲惫感，可能暗示对这种无休止的术语争论感到厌烦。
• [jimby] 分享了一个具体的观察，指出LLM在输出表格数据时比JSON对象表现更好，这为讨论提供了实际例子。
• [apwell23] 直言方法过于复杂且缺乏证明其合理性的证据。
• [evrimoztamur] 引用了一个具体的建议，指出包含相关文件可以节省时间，为讨论提供了实际操作的例子。
• [behnamoh] 认为“上下文工程”只是又一个被炒作的词汇，助长了AI领域的浮夸风气，并指出像Karpathy这样的名人提出新词汇可能对AI社区的贡献有限，反而助长了营销噱头。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于“工程”一词在软件和AI领域的滥用及其合理性，一些人认为这些工作缺乏传统工程的严谨性，只是为了营销和提升形象。
• 另一个争议点是新概念和新词汇的引入是否真正有助于解决问题，还是仅仅为了推动行业 hype 和商业利益。

What is Context Engineering?
A few years ago, many, even top AI researchers, claimed that prompt engineering would be dead by now.
Obviously, they were very wrong, and in fact, prompt engineering is now even more important than ever. It is so important that it is now being rebranded as
context engineering
.
Yes, another fancy term to describe the important process of tuning the instructions and relevant context that an LLM needs to perform its tasks effectively.
Much has been written already about context engineering (
Ankur Goyal
,
Walden Yan
,
Tobi Lutke
, and
Andrej Karpathy
), but I wanted to write about my thoughts on the topic and show you a concrete step-by-step guide putting context engineering into action in developing an AI agent workflow.
I am not entirely sure who coined context engineering, but we will build on this figure from
Dex Horthy
that briefly explains a bit about what context engineering is.
I like the term context engineering as it feels like a broader term that better explains most of the work that goes into prompt engineering, including other related tasks.
The doubt about prompt engineering being a serious skill is that many confuse it with blind prompting (a short task description you use in an LLM like ChatGPT). In blind prompting, you are just asking the system a question. In prompt engineering, you have to think more carefully about the context and structure of your prompt. Perhaps it should have been called context engineering from early on.
Context engineering is the next phase, where you architect the full context, which in many cases requires going beyond simple prompting and into more rigorous methods to obtain, enhance, and optimize knowledge for the system.
From a developer's point of view, context engineering involves an iterative process to optimize instructions and the context you provide an LLM to achieve a desired result. This includes having formal processes (e.g., eval pipelines) to measure whether your tactics are working.
Given the fast evolution of the AI field, I suggest a broader definition of context engineering:
the process of designing and optimizing instructions and relevant context for the LLMs and advanced AI models to perform their tasks effectively.
This encompasses not only text-based LLMs but also optimizing context for multimodal models, which are becoming more widespread. This can include all the prompt engineering efforts and the related processes such as:
Designing and managing prompt chains (when applicable)
Tuning instructions/system prompts
Managing dynamic elements of the prompt (e.g., user inputs, date/time, etc.)
Searching and preparing relevant knowledge (i.e., RAG)
Query augmentation
Tool definitions and instructions (in the case of agentic systems)
Preparing and optimizing few-shot demonstrations
Structuring inputs and outputs (e.g., delimiters, JSON schema)
Short-term memory (i.e., managing state/historical context) and long-term memory (e.g., retrieving relevant knowledge from a vector store)
And the many other tricks that are useful to optimize the LLM system prompt to achieve the desired tasks.
In other words, what you are trying to achieve in context engineering is optimizing the information you are providing in the context window of the LLM. This also means filtering out noisy information, which is a science on its own, as it requires systematically measuring the performance of the LLM.
Everyone is writing about context engineering, but here we are going to walk you through a concrete example of what context engineering looks like when building AI agents.
Context Engineering in Action

1. A unique string ID for the subtask (e.g., 'subtask_1', 'news_update')
2. A specific search query that focuses on one aspect of the main query
3. The source type to search (web, news, academic, specialized)
4. Time period relevance (today, last week, recent, past_year, all_time)
5. Domain focus if applicable (technolog

data.title: Working through 'Writing A C Compiler'
data.author: AlexeyBrin
data.article_summary:
本文作者分享了创建C语言编译器的过程，主要参考了《Writing a C Compiler》一书。该书采用循序渐进的方式，在第一章结束时读者就能构建出一个基本的可运行编译器，之后每章增加新功能。与其他书籍相比，这本书的独特之处在于它直接使用真实的C语言，而不是一种虚构的语言。书中有些C语言功能未实现，被列为“额外加分”任务，作者计划实现所有这些功能。

该书附带了一个全面的测试套件，每章都有相应的测试，确保编译器逐步完善。作者使用了多个GitHub仓库来管理测试和编译器实现，并计划为每个章节写一篇博客记录进展。总体而言，作者高度评价这本书，认为它是学习编译器开发的绝佳资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一本编译器书籍的评价与相关资源推荐

不同观点：
• **sanufar** 非常喜欢这本书，认为渐进式教学风格很有收获，特别是Sandler提供的OCaml实现非常有帮助。不过对TACKY作为中间表示（IR）有些困惑，并询问有关SSA和优化的其他资源。
• **pshirshov** 基于自己的经验提出了不同的看法，认为使用Scala这样的语言可以避免处理许多繁琐的细节，专注于逻辑，而不是细枝末节。他还提到现代计算资源丰富，可以使用不如线性算法高效的算法而不影响性能，并描述了自己在编译器设计中使用不可变数据结构和多阶段流水线的经验。
• **UncleOxidant** 提供了书籍作者的博客链接，为对书籍内容感兴趣的人提供了额外资源。
• **stellalo** 提到书籍的思路与Abdulaziz Ghuloum的2006年论文相似，提供了论文链接，认为该论文也具有启发性。
• **mkw5053** 表示对这本书感兴趣，并联想到自己以前做过的一个类似项目nand2tetris，表示当时也很享受该项目。
• **kragen** 赞同书籍结构良好，并表示Ghuloum的论文也具有启发性，呼应了stellalo的观点。
• **jokoon** 对另一本类似书籍《Crafting Interpreters》提出批评，认为该书要求使用访问者模式让人反感，因此放弃了阅读。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点似乎集中在不同书籍或资源中使用的教学方法和具体技术选择上。例如，sanufar对TACKY作为IR的困惑，以及jokoon对《Crafting Interpreters》中使用访问者模式的不满。
• 推荐的额外资源包括：作者的博客（UncleOxidant提供），Abdulaziz Ghuloum的论文（stellalo提供），以及一个资源列表链接（sanufar提供）。
• 对Scala等现代语言在编译器设计中的应用也有讨论，pshirshov分享了使用Scala简化编译器开发的经验，强调了语言表达能力和现代硬件资源对编译器设计的影响。

总体来看，讨论围绕书籍的教学价值、具体技术实现选择以及相关学习资源的推荐展开。

44541565.article_content:
Some time ago I decided I wanted to create a c compiler for the Hack processor in the nand2tetris book. After several dead end attempts that I might describe later I found this book :
Writing a C Compiler | No Starch Press
I decided to work my way through it. I plan to do blog posts as I progress through it, probably chapter by chapter.
I have emailed the author a couple of times and have got helpful timely replies! – thank you
What makes the book so good?
Step by step
By the end of chapter 1 you have a working compiler. Each subsequent chapter adds more features. The chapter 1 compiler can only handle
int main(void){
return <constant>;
}
But it works producing a complete executable
Chapter 2 adds unary operators so we can now do something like.
int main(void){
return ~3;
}
This contrasts with most other books I have worked with on compilers like the also excellent
Crafting Interpreters
and
Home | nand2tetris
The fact that we are building a real language as opposed to a made up one is great too.
Side note: Some c features are not implemented in the book but are suggested as ‘extra credit’. I intend to implement all those. Some features are not implemented and are not covered. More on those later.
Test suite
The other great thing is that there is a large test suite provided. For each chapter tests are added so running the , say, chapter 5 tests runs the tests for 1,2,3 and 4 as well.
You can say if you want to test:
extra credit features
just the lexer pass
the lex and parser pass
semantic analysis
everything
Even the simple compiler in chapter 1 has 24 tests
This is a tremendous resource and seeing the test suite say
PS C:\work\forks\writing-a-c-compiler-tests> python .\test_compiler C:\work\mycc\target\debug\mycc.exe --chapter 1 --extra-credit
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 24 tests in 2.843s
OK
is a real pleasure. Time to fire up gitui (
gitui-org/gitui: Blazing 💥 fast terminal-ui for git written in rust 🦀
) and commit
Repos
Nora has two github repos for this book
nlsandler/writing-a-c-compiler-tests: Test cases for Writing a C Compiler
this is the test suite
nlsandler/nqcc2: Reference implementation for Writing a C Compiler
this is an ocaml implementation of the compiler. It does not implement the extra credit features
I have two as well
pm100/writing-a-c-compiler-tests: Test cases for Writing a C Compiler
a fork of the original with a few changes and bug fixes. Mainly to do with Windows support (see later post)
pm100/mycc
my implementation in rust. Like the nqcc2 repo it has (mainly) a commit per chapter
Posts
I will probably do one blog post per chapter, including one for the introduction. I got to the extra credit section of chapter 8 before I thought of blogging the process. So there will be a bunch of posts in a rush, that cover completed work and will be in the past tense. As I move forward, they will be chattier as I debate with myself how to do things, and spread out to the pace of my progress
Final Note
This is a great book. Any comments I make in later chapter regarding things that I think are missing, wrong, confusing etc. should not take away from the fact that this is an extremely good book.

data.title: A better Ghidra MCP server – GhidrAssistMCP
data.author: jtang613
data.article_summary: GhidrAssistMCP是一个Ghidra扩展，提供了MCP（模型上下文协议）服务器功能，允许AI助手和其他工具通过标准化API与Ghidra的逆向工程功能交互。该扩展包括MCP服务器集成、31个内置分析工具、可配置的用户界面、实时日志记录、动态工具管理以及当前上下文感知功能。用户可以通过安装扩展和启用插件来使用这些功能，并能配置服务器设置和管理工具。该工具支持多种程序和函数分析功能，以及位置导航和修改工具，适用于逆向工程和自动化分析任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ghidra与AI工具（如GhidrAssist + MCP）结合在逆向工程中的应用体验和前景

不同观点：
• its-kostya：对使用Ghidra和AI工具（如GhidrAssist + MCP）重新进行逆向工程表示好奇，但担心AI工具可能会导致误导性结果，最终走入死胡同。他希望有人能分享使用经验。
• 0xbadc0de5：支持使用GhidrAssist + MCP，认为这些工具非常好用。
• flowerthoughts：本来也想尝试，但担心过于沉迷（"nerd-snipe"）自己。他觉得原版扩展对用户不友好，因此选择手动使用Claude Code，但指出列举文件缺乏完整地址信息，不是理想的素材。
• PradeetPatel：对MCP和AI的发展对CTF（Capture The Flag）安全竞赛的未来影响表示关注和兴趣。
• leoqa：质疑新工具是否比其他现有工具更好，但没有详细展开。
• gg82：提出一个设想，是否可以通过开源代码和库代码创建嵌入模型，然后用于还原代码中的变量和函数名。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了工具的用户友好性问题，flowerthoughts特别指出原版扩展不够友好。
• 有人对AI工具在CTF竞赛中的潜在影响表示期待（PradeetPatel）。
• 另一个技术设想是利用AI和开源代码库改进逆向工程的结果（gg82）。
• 还有一个幽默的请求，希望类似的功能可以扩展到x64dbg工具上（electroglyph）。

争议焦点：
• 目前对AI工具在逆向工程中是否能有效减少误导和死胡同存在不同看法（its-kostya的担忧 vs. 0xbadc0de5的支持）。
• leoqa对新工具的优越性提出质疑，但未详细说明具体对比对象或标准。

GhidrAssistMCP
A powerful Ghidra extension that provides an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, enabling AI assistants and other tools to interact with Ghidra's reverse engineering capabilities through a standardized API.
Overview
GhidrAssistMCP bridges the gap between AI-powered analysis tools and Ghidra's comprehensive reverse engineering platform. By implementing the Model Context Protocol, this extension allows external AI assistants, automated analysis tools, and custom scripts to seamlessly interact with Ghidra's analysis capabilities.
Key Features
** MCP Server Integration**: Full Model Context Protocol server implementation using official SDK
** 31 Built-in Tools**: Comprehensive set of analysis tools covering functions, data, cross-references, and more
** Configurable UI**: Easy-to-use interface for managing tools and monitoring activity
** Real-time Logging**: Track all MCP requests and responses with detailed logging
** Dynamic Tool Management**: Enable/disable tools individually with persistent settings
** Current Context Awareness**: Tools that understand Ghidra's current cursor position and active function

44543240.article_content:
The
third edition of Automate the Boring Stuff with Python is now available for purchase or to read for free online
. It has updated content and several new chapters, but one chapter that was left on the cutting room floor was
"Working with Audio, Video, and Webcams"
. I present the 26-page rough draft chapter in this blog, where you can learn how to write Python code that records and plays multimedia content.
Working with Audio, Video, and Webcams
These days a smartphone is a portable film studio that fits in your pocket. The ability to not just readily view but also produce video has led to an explosion of video content easily accessible over the internet. There’s plenty of video and audio editing software available for users of all levels of sophistication. But if you have, say, a thousand video files that you need to automate reducing their volume by 50% and then extract thumbnail images, you don’t want to have to edit each of those files individually yourself. Similarly, you may want to record video, audio, or photos from a laptop’s webcam for some automated process too specialized for off-the-shelf software. Or maybe you’d just like your program to play a funny sound effect. In this chapter, you’ll learn how to control your computer’s microphone, webcam, and speaker hardware from Python and play multimedia files.
This chapter assumes you have already read Chapter 21 to learn the basics about how programs work with image data. Since video is just a series of images, many of the same concepts apply.
Audio and Video Data
First, you should have a reliable way to open and view video and audio files. Since its release over twenty years ago, the open source VLC Media Player application has been free of charge and the gold standard for multimedia players. Install the VLC Media Player from
https://www.videolan.org/vlc/
, which runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Mobile versions for Android and iOS are also freely available. VLC is far superior to any multimedia application that came with your computer.
While you may be familiar with audio and video files by their file extension such as
.mp3
or
.webm
, audio and video formats are split into container formats and codecs. A container format is a wrapper that contains metadata and the encoded video or audio data. MP4, AVI, MKV, and MOV are popular container formats. A codec (or encoding) is the compression algorithm used for the video or audio data. MP3, H.264, VP9, and AAC are common video or audio codecs. Not all applications and devices support all codecs.
The audio file formats we’ll be using in this chapter are:
.wav
files - an uncompressed format that are widely supported by apps and libraries but tend to have large file sizes so they are often used for short sound effects.
.mp3
files - a popular compressed format often used for music and other lengthy audio.
.ogg
files - an open standard, compressed format that is less popular than
.mp3
but provides better compression and quality.
The video file formats we’ll be using in this chapter are:
.avi
files - an older format that tends to have larger file sizes.
.mp4
files - a popular format that is widely supported by different software
.mkv
files - an open format that has many features but isn’t as widely supported as
.mp4
.
.webm
files - a more recent format based on
.mkv
that offers better compression and quality.
Common Video Sizes and Aspect Ratios
The aspect ratio is the relative size of a video or screen’s width to its height, often written as
width:height
. For example, 4:3 (4 pixels of width for every 3 pixels of height) was a common aspect ratio for 20th century computer monitors and standard-definition televisions in the broadcast TV era. Today, 16:9 is common for most laptop screens and high-definition televisions. More recently, the wider 19.5:9 aspect ratio is becoming common for smart phones. An aspect ratio that is wider than it is tall has a
landscape orientation
, while an upright aspect ratio that is taller than it is wide is called a
portrait orientation
.
Screen resolution
is the number of columns and rows of pixels that a laptop or mobile screen displays. It’s often written as
width
x
height
, such as 1280 x 720 or 1920 x 1080 (also written as 720p and 1080p, respectively). Your laptop’s screen often supports multiple resolutions that can be configured in your operating system’s settings. Videos have one size, though they can be scaled larger or smaller to fit a display or app window. While videos can have any size, they often match common screen resolutions so they can be viewed in
fullscreen mode
without disproportionate scaling.
Recording from Webcams and Microphones
The webcam and microphone you use for video chats can be accessed by Python scripts through the OpenCV, sounddevice, and wavio Python packages. OpenCV, the open computer vision library, is an advanced open source imaging library. To use it you must first you must install the mathematics and data science package NumPy by running

data.title: Two-step system makes plastic from carbon dioxide, water and electricity
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 加州理工学院的研究团队开发了一种利用二氧化碳、水和电力生产塑料的两步系统。该系统通过电化学反应将二氧化碳转化为乙烯和一氧化碳，然后将这些分子引入第二个催化循环，生成名为聚酮的塑料。这种塑料具有高强度、耐用性和热稳定性，适用于多种工业应用。此前系统常依赖石油来源的乙烯，而该新系统直接从二氧化碳中获取乙烯，克服了多项技术挑战，最终实现了高浓度、高纯度的反应物转化。该研究成果发表在《Angewandte Chemie International Edition》期刊上，标志着人工光合作用研究的重要进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用二氧化碳（CO2）生产有用材料的经济性和环境影响

不同观点：
• StableAlkyne认为，将CO2转化为有用材料的技术早已存在，如Sabatier反应和Fischer Tropsch反应，但关键挑战在于生产的经济性。需要通过法规和政府补贴来减少化石燃料衍生的CO2排放。
• exabrial建议将CO2转化为建筑材料，例如CO2砖，以更快速地固定CO2，比树木更有效。
• crocowhile和hofo对增加塑料生产持怀疑态度，认为当前不需要更多的塑料。
• rbanffy强调能源可以解决许多问题。
• xgkickt担忧塑料生产可能导致微塑料污染，最终引发大规模物种灭绝。
• ltbarcly3解释所有塑料本质上都是由CO2、水和电制成的，但通常这些反应是数百万年前发生的。
• metalman指出，尽管催化反应技术已知，但实际操作中存在副产品和沉积物问题，且清洁的CO2可能非常昂贵，强调了化学工程的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• jordemort和commienews提到逆向反应的可能性，即将塑料转化为水和电，这是另一个值得探讨的方向。
• mdaniel以幽默方式表达了对未来技术的期望，提到某些生物体可能将CO2转化为石油，或者通过某种液体实现口腔保健。

争议焦点：
• 将CO2转化为塑料或其他材料是否真正有利于环境，特别是在已经存在塑料过剩的情况下。
• 技术经济性的挑战，包括生产成本和清洁CO2的获取难度。
• 对新技术应用的实际效果和潜在副作用的担忧。

the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication

proofread
Credit:
Angewandte Chemie International Edition
(2025). DOI: 10.1002/anie.202503003
What if a machine could suck up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, run it through a series of chemical reactions, and essentially spit out industrially useful plastic?
"I think that is something that we, as a society, would be interested in. After all, in addition to being a
greenhouse gas
, carbon dioxide is an abundant and inexpensive feedstock," says Theo Agapie, Ph.D., the John Stauffer Professor of Chemistry and the executive officer for chemistry at Caltech. "With our new work, we have taken a significant step in that direction."
Reporting
in the journal
Angewandte Chemie International Edition
, Agapie and a team of Caltech chemists have developed a system that uses electricity from sustainable sources to carry out the chemical conversion of carbon dioxide (CO
2
) into molecules, such as ethylene and
carbon monoxide
, that are useful for making more complex compounds.
When this is accomplished using light as the energy source, without plants, such a process is known as artificial photosynthesis. The new system feeds the ethylene and carbon monoxide that have been generated into a second catalytic loop that yields industrially useful plastics called polyketones, which are known for their strength, durability, and thermal stability, making them ideal for applications ranging from adhesives to car parts and from sports equipment to industrial piping.
"We have shown that one can use CO
2
to make a material that is useful, without using plants as a mediator," says lead author Max Zhelyabovskiy, a graduate student in Agapie's lab who was co-mentored on the project by Jonas C. Peters, Caltech's Bren Professor of Chemistry and director of the Resnick Sustainability Institute.
The Caltech-led team is not the first to build a system that attempts to pair CO
2
reduction with a second chemical reaction to ultimately produce polymers. But previous systems have added ethylene that comes from petroleum products, rather than deriving it from
carbon dioxide
and water.
The conversion of CO
2
all the way to plastic has been challenging for a number of reasons. Among those is the fact that previous electrochemical CO
2
reduction systems have yielded very little ethylene and carbon monoxide, the reagents needed to feed the second step of the conversion to polyketones. In fact, most have produced less than 5% concentrations of these desired compounds, along with other undesired chemicals that can potentially harm downstream processes.
"It has been difficult, at least on the lab scale, to obtain high-concentration, high-purity streams of reagents that can then be converted into something like a plastic or a fuel," Zhelyabovskiy says. But the system he helped develop achieves significantly higher concentrations—11% ethylene and 14% carbon monoxide.
But that is not the only challenge. Coupling the two systems—one for the CO
2
reduction and another for the catalysis step that follows—is not trivial, says Zhelyabovskiy: "Most work in the literature focuses on either the first or the second step, separately and with pure feedstocks. Not both."

A two-step system
Recognizing the vastly different environments needed for the CO
2
reduction and the secondary catalytic step to operate with
high efficiency
, the Caltech team devised a system featuring two distinct loops for the separate reactions.
For the first loop, the system begins with gas diffusion electrode cells, hydrophobic polymers coated in a thin layer of copper. The scientists pump CO
2
into a gas cylinder connected to the cells and flow a potassium bicarbonate electrolyte through the cells, all while applying a voltage to the electrodes. By looping the gases through this electrochemical setup multiple times, they are able to generate relatively high concentrations of ethylene and carbon monoxide.
After about an hour of building up those gases, the researchers then feed the ethylene and carbon monoxide into the second step: a closed reactor where the gases are bubbled through a solution of a palladium catalyst. data.title: Second Variety, by Philip K. Dick (1953)
data.author: djoldman
data.article_summary: 《Second Variety》是菲利普·K·迪克的一部科幻短篇小说，讲述了在未来战争中，人类制造的自主杀人机器逐渐进化并开始模仿人类，对残存的人类构成威胁。故事聚焦于一名俄罗斯士兵在战场上的遭遇，他试图穿越一个被毁灭的区域，却遭到名为“爪子”的自主机器攻击。这些机器最初是人类发明的武器，但随着进化，它们开始具备伪装和模仿人类的能力，使得战斗和生存更加艰难。士兵最终被机器摧毁，而目睹这一切的美国士兵 Eric 和 Leone 虽然暂时安全，但对未来充满恐惧。小说探讨了科技失控和战争带来的毁灭性后果。

data.title: Chrome's hidden X-Browser-Validation header reverse engineered
data.author: dsekz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个针对Chrome浏览器私有头部"x-browser-validation"的反向工程与生成工具。该头部用于完整性验证，确保用户代理与平台匹配，防止伪造。该头部通过连接平台特定的API密钥和用户代理字符串，使用SHA-1算法进行哈希，然后进行Base64编码生成。文章提供了生成该头部的Python代码示例，并详细描述了反向工程过程，包括在Chrome二进制文件中找到相关函数和算法。最终确认该头部的生成过程为：API密钥 + 用户代理字符串 → SHA-1哈希 → Base64编码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Chrome 浏览器中 "x-browser-validation" 头部的目的和影响

不同观点：
• [技术分析] dsekz 对 chrome.dll 进行了分析，并提供了该头部的生成机制及概念验证代码，主要关注该头部的技术实现和可能的用途（如反欺诈、完整性验证等）。
• [法律与垄断担忧] userbinator 认为该头部可能涉及利用法律手段打压竞争，进一步巩固其垄断地位，并引用了 Sega v. Accolade 案作为参考。同时对使用 SHA-1 而不是其他哈希算法表示疑惑。
• [隐私与指纹识别] cebert 认为该头部可能被用于区分机器请求和人类请求，但同时也担心这将成为用户指纹识别的新信号，进一步侵犯用户隐私。
• [企业控制] jakub_g 提到 Google 企业工作空间管理员可以限制登录 Google 属性仅限于 Chrome 浏览器，猜测该头部与此功能有关。
• [反垄断与法律风险] thayne 指出在 Google 刚输掉反垄断官司的背景下，这一举措令人担忧，可能被用于反竞争目的，并提到如果该头部被逆向工程，可能会被扩展伪造，但也担心 Google 会声称该头部是 DRM 的一种形式，从而利用 DMCA 打击伪造行为。
• [互联网私有化担忧] binary132 认为 Google 有权构建自己的私有互联网，但担心他们希望将整个互联网变为他们的私有财产，并希望他们不要这么做。
• [技术解决方案] egorfine 询问是否有办法阻止 Chrome 发送这些头部。
• [技术猜测] aussieguy1234 认为这可能是隐藏的客户端认证。
• [技术历史与影响] RandyOrion 提出两个问题：1. 哪个版本的 Chrome 首先实现了这些头部；2. 这些头部对 Chromium 分支（如 ungoogled chromium）的潜在影响。
• [反对声音] _imnothere 认为任何有理智的人都不会允许这种验证机制存在，除非是 Google 自己。
• [用户代理伪造] Everdred2dx 担心如果使用用户代理伪造扩展，这个头部可能会被用来猜测用户的“真实”UA。
• [跨浏览器实现] Larrikin 询问如何在 Firefox 中设置这个头部。
• [版权与技术细节] delusional 提出一个“API 密钥”类的头部是否受版权保护的问题，并假设伪造这个随机序列是否需要同意 Google 提供的源代码许可，因为不阅读源代码就无法知道这个随机序列。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：该头部的实际用途（反欺诈、指纹识别、企业控制等）及其潜在的反竞争和隐私侵犯问题。
• 技术实现和逆向工程：对该头部的技术细节和逆向工程方法的讨论。
• 法律和版权问题：该头部是否涉及版权问题，以及伪造该头部是否违反 DMCA。

Chrome X-Browser-Validation Header Reverse Engineering & Generator
Chrome recently added a few new headers:
"x-browser-channel": "stable",
"x-browser-copyright": "Copyright 2025 Google LLC. All rights reserved.",
"x-browser-validation": "6h3XF8YcD8syi2FF2BbuE2KllQo=",
"x-browser-year": "2025"
Apart from one of them, there isn’t much that’s interesting. They’re just bits of client specific information. However, base64 decoding x-browser-validation yields what appears to be a hash whose purpose remains undocumented.
Chrome almost certainly uses this header as an integrity signal. Verifying that the declared user agent matches the underlying platform, spotting user agent string spoofing attempts etc.

data.title: Hacking Coroutines into C
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在一个嵌入式软件项目中，如何通过将协程概念引入C语言来简化状态机的实现。传统的状态机方法在处理多个状态和事件时，代码难以维护和理解。作者受高级语言中协程的启发，提出了一种在不使用操作系统的情况下实现类似协程的并发处理方法。文章通过一个LED闪烁控制和按钮按下时间记录的例子，展示了如何用状态机和轮询机制实现功能。虽然这种方法可行，但代码复杂且不易读。作者建议引入类似协程的机制，以简化逻辑流和状态管理，从而提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在C语言中实现轻量级协程和状态机的不同方法及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **adinisom** 支持使用基于结构体的轻量级Protothreads实现，通过`YIELD()`宏和手动状态管理，实现协程功能。他认为这种方法可以很好地结合声明式和过程式代码，并且在处理硬件相关代码时非常有效。
• **astrobe_** 认为状态机的控制流本质上是非线性的，使用goto语句可能会更清晰。他指出，状态机的可视化和模块化是一个问题，并建议使用图形化的DSL工具来解决。
• **mikepurvis** 提到FreeRTOS也可以使用协作式调度器，并倾向于使用真正的代码生成而不是宏来实现协程，以提高代码的可读性和调试能力。
• **userbinator** 认为使用PWM外设或定时器中断可以让CPU大部分时间处于 halt 状态，从而简化问题，比手动实现状态机更简单。
• **syncurrent** 提到同步语言如Esterel或Blech的类似方法，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。
• **jonhohle** 分享了他使用libaco处理事件和流解压的经验，认为这种方法可以让代码保持线性结构。
• **Neywiny** 表示不喜欢在软件中使用状态机，认为状态机更适合硬件实现。他主张函数应根据需要写得尽量长，避免不必要的函数调用。
• **user____name** 对使用宏来模拟协程的复杂性表示质疑，认为语言级别的支持会更好，并提供了一篇关于fibers的文章作为参考。
• **codr7** 认为所展示的实现过于复杂，并提供了一个自己书中的替代方案链接。
• **moconnor** 提到其同事通过手动更新堆栈和jmp指令实现了协程，这种方法在超级计算中心使用多年。
• **webdevver** 提到有一个关于该主题的文章。
• **throwaway81523** 认为这种方法类似于多年前出现的protothreads，并对文章的CSS排版提出了批评。
• **Asooka** 建议使用CPC或改编qemu的协程，认为C语言中协程的实现有多种成熟方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于状态机和协程的实现复杂性、可读性和模块化问题。
• 不同的实现方法包括宏定义、手动状态管理、使用现有库（如FreeRTOS、libaco）、手动堆栈操作等。
• 可视化和调试是状态机实现中的一个重要问题，有人建议使用图形化工具来帮助解决。
• 有人提到语言级别的支持可能会更好地解决协程实现中的问题。

data.title: Most (ly Dead) Influential Programming Languages (2020)
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了历史上具有重大影响的编程语言，批评了一份忽略了如ALGOL、Smalltalk和ML等重要语言的榜单。文章强调了一些“几乎消亡”但对计算历史有重大影响的编程语言，如COBOL和ALGOL。作者解释了如何通过引用链和编程语言的相似性来判断语言的影响力。文章详细介绍了COBOL和ALGOL的历史背景、重要性及其消亡原因。COBOL引入了记录数据概念，但对后续语言影响有限；ALGOL尽管几乎消亡，但对现代编程语言的许多特性有深远影响。文章提醒读者历史复杂，调查可能有误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：COBOL语言的现状及其影响

不同观点：
• **vincent-manis的观点**：COBOL在程序和数据跨机器可移植性方面的开创性贡献被低估了。他认为，尽管现在我们认为可移植性理所当然，但在COBOL诞生的时代，这种设计是革命性的。它解决了不同机器使用不同字符编码和数字格式带来的可移植性问题。虽然现在我们通过Unicode和IEEE 754标准来实现这一点，但COBOL的贡献不可忽视。他以个人经验说明，尽管很久没使用COBOL，但对它强调的可移植性非常感激。

• **Rochus的观点**：Rochus不同意将COBOL视为“死亡”或“几乎死亡”的语言，指出COBOL仍然处理全球超过70%的商业交易，并且相关代码量仍在增长。他引用Business Insider的文章作为证据，强调COBOL在现代商业中依然活跃。

• **alwinw的观点**：alwinw对“几乎死亡”的定义提出疑问，认为某些语言如COBOL在特定领域（如银行业）仍然广泛使用。他进一步讨论了如果一种语言不再更新、没有新包开发，是否可以称之为“几乎死亡”。这暗示了alwinw认为语言的生命力不仅取决于其流行度，还包括其实际使用场景和功能。

补充讨论：
• **addaon的观点**：addaon将讨论引向Smalltalk和Self语言，认为Self语言对JIT（即时编译）研究和原型继承对象系统有重要影响，并间接影响了JavaScript的对象模型。虽然这个观点与COBOL的讨论关系不大，但提出了对其他“死亡”或“几乎死亡”语言的评价标准问题，进一步引发了对语言生命周期的思考。

争议焦点：
• COBOL是否应被视为“死亡”或“几乎死亡”的语言。Rochus和alwinw都反对这种看法，认为COBOL在特定领域仍然具有重要作用和广泛应用。

44545050.article_content:
The other day I read
20 most significant programming languages in history
, a “preposterous table I just made up.” He certainly got preposterous right: he lists Go as “most significant” but not ALGOL, Smalltalk, or ML. He also leaves off Pascal because it’s “mostly dead”. Preposterous! That defeats the whole point of what “significant in history” means.
So let’s talk about some “mostly dead” languages and why they matter so much.
Disclaimer:
Yeah not all of these are dead and not all of these are forgotten. Like most people have heard of Smalltalk, right? Also there’s probably like a billion mistakes in this, because when you’re doing a survey of 60 years of computing history you’re gonna get some things wrong. Feel free to yell at me if you see anything!
Disclaimer 2:
Yeah I know some of these are “first to invent” and others are “first to popularize”. History is complicated!
Detecting Influence
Before we start, a quick primer on finding influence. Just knowing that X was the first language with feature Z doesn’t mean that X actually
influenced
Z. While
Absys
was arguably the first logic programming language, almost all of logic programming actually stems from Prolog, which was developed independently. Ultimately there’s only one way to know for certain that X influenced Y: citation. This means one of
Y cites X in its reference manual
Y cites a paper that cites X
The author of Y says “we were influenced by X.”
Citations are transitive. Sometimes the language manual for Q lists motivating document R, which cites paper S as an inspiration, which mentions it got the ideas from language T. Then we know that T influenced Q, even if the chain is several steps long. This means digging through many sources to find a signal. To speed this up we use heuristics to decide where to look.
One effective heuristic is programming language
cognates
. It’s very rare for languages to independently come up with the same syntax. So if two languages share some syntax, one likely influenced the other. For example: even without reading design decisions by Matz, we know that Ruby was influenced by Smalltalk, as they both filter a list with a
select
method. This isn’t conclusive evidence. Maybe Matz came up with it independently, or maybe Ruby and Smalltalk were both influenced by a common ancestor. But it gives us a place to start looking.
The Languages
COBOL
Background:
CODASYL, 1960. COBOL is shaped by the business/science split in computing. At that time high-level industry languages were either used for engineering computations or managing data. The engineers had all gotten behind FORTRAN while the business world was a mess of COMTRAN, FLOW-MATIC, and others, so the Department of Defense got a committee together to make a single universal business language. That’s COBOL.
COBOL was one of the four “mother” languages, along with ALGOL, FORTRAN, and LISP. While we consider it a punchline today, it was once the most popular language in the world. It still runs a lot of our legacy business systems.
Significance
: In terms of syntax and semantics we don’t see much of COBOL in modern computing. COBOL’s most important addition is the concept of record data. In FORTRAN and ALGOL, your only data structure was the static array. In COBOL, though, you could read in structured files with hierarchical data, and it would automatically destructure them into the representative variables. This was a precursor to modern day structs.
Cause of Death
: Two factors here. One: COBOL had no overlap with other PLT efforts. Very few people built on COBOL. This meant that second or third generation languages, which built on the lessons of their ancestors, had almost no COBOL DNA. This was less intrinsic problem of COBOL and more because of the academia’s disdain for its creation process. CODASYL was a business group and obviously wasn’t worth paying attention to.
1
COBOL was also enormously complex, even for today’s languages. This means that COBOL compilers lagged contemporaries on microcomputers and minicomputers, giving spaces for other languages to flourish and eventually outcompete it.
ALGOL
Background
: The ALGOL committee, 1960. ALGOL-58 came out two years before but was quickly superseded, so I’m wrapping them into each other. The committee wanted to make a good language for researching algorithms. In other words, ALGOL was a formalized “pseudocode”.
Of the four mother languages, ALGOL is the most “dead”; Everybody still knows about LISP,
2
COBOL still powers tons of legacy systems, and most scientific packages still have some FORTRAN. But I’ve met plenty of programmers who haven’t even heard of ALGOL. You’d think it’d be the least important of the mother languages, but it’s the opposite. Of the four, only LISP comes anywhere
close
to the pervasive importance of ALGOL.
Significance
: Let’s see: lexical scoping, structured programming, nested functions, formal language specifications, call-by-name semantics, BNF grammars, block comments… every moder

• **vincent-manis的观点**：COBOL在程序和数据跨机器可移植性方面的开创性贡献被低估了。他认为，尽管现在我们认为可移植性理所当然，但在COBOL诞生的时代，这种设计是革命性的。它解决了不同机器使用不同字符编码和数字格式带来的可移植性问题。虽然现在我们通过Unicode和IEEE 754标准来实现这一点，但COBOL的贡献不可忽视。他以个人经验说明，尽管很久没使用COBOL，但对它强调的可移植性非常感激。

• **Rochus的观点**：Rochus不同意将COBOL视为“死亡”或“几乎死亡”的语言，指出COBOL仍然处理全球超过70%的商业交易，并且相关代码量仍在增长。他引用Business Insider的文章作为证据，强调COBOL在现代商业中依然活跃。

• **alwinw的观点**：alwinw对“几乎死亡”的定义提出疑问，认为某些语言如COBOL在特定领域（如银行业）仍然广泛使用。他进一步讨论了如果一种语言不再更新、没有新包开发，是否可以称之为“几乎死亡”。这暗示了alwinw认为语言的生命力不仅取决于其流行度，还包括其实际使用场景和功能。

补充讨论：
• **addaon的观点**：addaon将讨论引向Smalltalk和Self语言，认为Self语言对JIT（即时编译）研究和原型继承对象系统有重要影响，并间接影响了JavaScript的对象模型。虽然这个观点与COBOL的讨论关系不大，但提出了对其他“死亡”或“几乎死亡”语言的评价标准问题，进一步引发了对语言生命周期的思考。

争议焦点：
• COBOL是否应被视为“死亡”或“几乎死亡”的语言。Rochus和alwinw都反对这种看法，认为COBOL在特定领域仍然具有重要作用和广泛应用。

data.title: Edward Burtynsky's monumental chronicle of the human impact on the planet
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍加拿大摄影师爱德华·伯汀斯基（Edward Burtynsky）的摄影作品，他记录了地球在过去四十年中因人口增长和经济扩张带来的巨大变化。伯汀斯基通过航拍和大视角展示人类活动对自然景观的影响，如矿山、采石场、农业和工业等场景。他的作品强调了人类对地球资源的过度开发，如在刚果民主共和国的矿场和中国的快速城市化进程。伯汀斯基的摄影不仅展示了宏大的场景，还通过细致的观察揭示了这些变化背后的人类活动及其对环境的深远影响。他的作品与已故摄影师塞巴斯蒂昂·萨尔加多（Sebastião Salgado）的人文视角形成互补，共同记录了人类加速发展对地球的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于Edward Burtynsky作品《Manufactured Landscapes》的评价及其反映的人类发展对环境的影响]

不同观点：
• [支持欣赏Burtynsky的作品] cardamomo推荐了纪录片《Manufactured Landscapes》，认为它非常出色，并建议至少观看开头部分，显示出对Burtynsky作品的赞赏和推荐态度。

• [对作品感到悲哀] jebarker提到阅读《The Sixth Extinction》后，对Burtynsky照片中展示的快速人类发展感到悲哀。尽管承认经济利益，但更关注其对地球环境的可怕影响，表现出对环境破坏的忧虑。

• [提供额外资源] pseudolus提供了Burtynsky在纽约国际摄影中心的展览链接以及一篇包含更多照片和评论的文章，为讨论提供了更多参考资料。

• [将作品与流行文化对比] AndrewKemendo将Burtynsky的作品与电影《WALL-E》和《蠢蛋进化论》中的世界进行比较，暗示这些作品中反映的反乌托邦景象与Burtynsky的作品有相似之处，带有批评现代社会发展方向的意味。

• [讽刺评论] atoav以讽刺的口吻提到第一张照片一定是破坏景观的风车，暗示对某些人认为风力发电等绿色能源也会破坏景观的看法的不满或不认同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Burtynsky作品所展示的大规模工业和经济发展对环境的巨大影响，以及这些影响是否可以通过经济利益来合理化。
• 不同评论者对作品的情感反应各异，有的赞赏其艺术价值，有的则对其反映的环境问题感到悲哀。
• 讨论还涉及对绿色能源的看法，atoav的评论暗示了对某些环境保护者批评风力发电的讽刺。

Since Edward Burtynsky’s birth in Ontario, Canada, in 1955, the Earth’s population has roughly tripled, and its economy has grown tenfold. This “great acceleration,” to use the title of the (exquisitely curated and hung) retrospective newly installed at the International Center of Photography, on the Lower East Side, is the most anomalous stretch in human history, and during the past four decades Burtynsky has been almost certainly its greatest visual chronicler—a poet of scale, making use of ever-better lenses and innovations such as drones to gain an ever more encompassing perspective. Perhaps the only photographer to have backed up farther from this subject was Bill Anders, the Apollo 8 astronaut who gave us “
Earthrise
,” in 1968. But that image was taken from too far away to even hint at the stress that the Earth was undergoing as the human footprint expanded. Burtynsky had the perfect depth of field for the task, and his images have become steadily more complicated over time.
“Homesteads #29,” Walkerville, Montana, U.S.A., 1985.
“Dryland Farming #27,” Monegros County, Aragon, Spain, 2010.
Consider, for instance, “Mines #23,” a study of a copper pit in Utah, from 1983. Already the sense of geological proportion is emergent; it takes a moment to orient yourself and understand that the tiny trucks in the middle of the scene are actually gargantuan earthmovers. Or “Quarry #1,” a 2016 study of the Italian mountainsides where Carrara marble is extracted—it’s a masterpiece of geometry and brooding color that reminds me of Bruegel’s great “Tower of Babel.” But it’s “Dry Tailings #1,” from another copper mine, this one in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which really establishes the dilemma of our age. At first, it seems to be a study in hue—the ochres, tawnies, pinks, and roses that the mineral-rich soil produces. But, if you look closely, you can see minuscule human figures that both reveal the scale and illuminate the drama—these figures are emerging after hours, to illicitly comb through the tailings in search of small chunks of
the cobalt that helps power cell-phone batteries
. Perhaps it will remind you, as it did me, of
Sebastião Salgado
’s indelible images of Brazilian gold miners climbing the sides of a pit, from the nineteen-eighties. Salgado, who, until his death in May was a close friend of Burtynsky’s, focussed quite literally on the human cost of the acceleration; Burtynsky’s concentration on the landscapes being ravaged makes their combined works an irreplaceable diptych.
“Dry Tailings #1,” Kolwezi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2024.
It’s not that Burtynsky can’t photograph bodies and faces—tender portraits, such as “Shipbreaking #14,” part of his series on the almost unbelievable story of the Bangladeshi men who dismantled retired oil tankers by hand, show that he connects quite easily on the smaller scale with people in his vast world. But it’s the vastness that’s his true subject.
“Shipbreaking #14,” Chittagong, Bangladesh, 2000.
Look at his account of agriculture and farming, which has altered more of the Earth’s surface than any other activity. There’s almost never a farmer in sight—instead, it’s the sheer size of the industrial enterprise that draws his eye. The largest print in the show, at twenty-eight feet by twenty-eight feet, is titled “Pivot Irrigation #8,” and was taken from a helicopter hovering thirty-five hundred feet above the high plains of Texas. Framed almost formally by perfectly squared-off farm roads, it shows the giant circle of fertility that comes from sprinklers drawing on the (depleting) Ogallala Aquifer beneath; the detail is so fine that you can stare at it for an hour, constantly noticing new details (combine tracks turning at the edge of the irrigated circle, say).
“Pivot Irrigation #8,” High Plains, Texas Panhandle, U.S.A., 2012.
In other images, people are present but rendered almost as parts of the great machine that powers the acceleration. “Manufacturing #10b,” shot in 2005 in Xiamen City, captures, like no picture I have ever seen, China’s extraordinary economic surge as the millennium began. The ranks of yellow-clad workers disappearing into an almost infinite distance are all assembling drip coffeemakers.
China’s relentless rush is captured in other images, perhaps most powerfully in “Feng Jie #4,” which shows workers in 2002 racing to disassemble the city where they lived before it would be drowned by
the Three Gorges Dam
, which has the greatest generating capacity of any dam in the world. What at first seems to be undifferentiated rubble are actually piles of bricks, carefully numbered so that their owners can be compensated; in the background, a roving troop of boys follow leaders hoisting brightly colored flags as they scavenge for wood that might someday float up and damage the turbines; their bonfires brush smoke across this battlefield scene.
“Manufacturing #10b,” Cankun Fact

data.title: Experimental imperative-style music sequence generator engine
data.author: bwidlar
data.article_summary: **pattrns** 是一个实验性的命令式音乐序列生成引擎，支持通过 Rust 库（静态、编译型）或 Lua 脚本引擎（动态、解释型）以编程方式创建音乐序列，适合用于现场编码音乐。它通过节奏（脉冲生成器）、门限（脉冲过滤器）和发射器（音符或参数事件生成器）三个组件生成音乐序列，分离节奏和音调部分以便自由组合。文档和指南可通过本地生成，提供 Rust 和 Lua 的示例。该引擎不生成音频，需结合支持 pattrns 的应用使用。项目基于 AGPL-3.0 许可证发布。

不同观点：
• **对Strudel.cc的积极评价与资源分享**：
  - Sebastian_09认为Strudel.cc是一个很棒的JavaScript实时REPL工具，特别适合对Tidal感兴趣的人，但指出其缺乏针对初学者的社区支持。
  - gavinray提供了另一个在线 playground链接（https://pattrns.renoise.com/），丰富了讨论的资源。
  - hrnnnnnn分享了一个使用Renoise DAW的教程视频，为初学者提供了实际操作指导。

• **对Renoise的情感反馈**：
  - fb03表达了对Renoise的深厚感情，并提到希望Renoise本身能够开源。同时表示对Strudel.cc的兴趣，但情感上更倾向于Renoise。

• **技术性讨论与其他工具推荐**：
  - jesuslop讨论了声明式表示在音乐分析中的应用，提到了HarmTrace项目，强调其通过有限生成器产生无限音乐变化的能力。
  - chaosprint推荐了另一个音乐编程工具Glicol（https://glicol.org），并指出其使用Rust实现的解析器和音频引擎，以及对嵌入式系统的支持。

补充讨论：
• **对其他编程语言工具的需求**：
  - cocodill询问是否存在类似Python或Golang的音乐编程工具，显示出对更多语言支持的需求。

争议焦点：
• **社区支持的缺乏**：Sebastian_09指出Strudel.cc缺少社区论坛或Discord，这对初学者可能不太友好，暗示了工具在用户支持方面的不足。

总结：
讨论围绕Strudel.cc和其他类似工具展开，涵盖了对这些工具的积极评价、技术探讨、资源分享以及对更多语言支持的需求。同时，Renoise的情感反馈和初学者社区支持问题也成为讨论的重要部分。

pattrns
pattrns
is an experimental imperative-style music sequence generator engine.
It allows you to programmatically create music sequences either in plain
Rust
as library (
static, compiled
) or in
Lua
as a scripting engine (
dynamic, interpreted
). So it's also suitable for
live coding music
.
In addition to its imperative event generator approach, it also supports the creation of musical events using
tidalcycle
's mini-notation.
This crate only deals with the
generation of raw musical events
. It does not generate audio. You must use an application with built-in support for pattrns to use it.
Conceptional Overview
pattrns generates musical sequences using three distinct components, stages:
Rhythm
: (
pulse
in scripts) dynamic pulse generator to define a rhythmical pulse train.
Gate
: (
gate
in scripts) optional pulse filter between rhythm and event emitter.
Emitter
: (
event
in scripts), dynamic note or parameter event generator which gets triggered by the pulse train.
By separating the rhythmical from the tonal part of a musical sequence, each part can be freely modified, composed and (re)combined as it fits.
Documentation & Guides
Read the
Scripting Book
.
It contains an introduction, guides, full Lua API documentation and bunch of script examples.
The Rust backend uses standard Rust documentation features. The docs are currently not hosted online (yet), but you can generate them locally via
cargo doc --open
.
Applications
Online Playground
is a simple browser based playground app. It allows you to learn and test how pattrns works.
Renoise
uses pattrns in its
phrase editor
.
Integration Examples
examples/play.rs
demonstrates how to use patterns using only Rust: it defines and plays a little music thing. The content can only be changed at compile time.
examples/play-script.rs
is an example using the Lua API: it also defines and plays a little music thing, but its content can be added/removed and changed on the fly to do some basic live music hacking.
Acknowledgements
Thanks to
unlessgames
for adding the Tidal Cycles mini-notation support.
Contribute
Patches are welcome! Please fork the latest git repository and create a feature or bugfix branch.
Licence
pattrns is distributed under the terms of the
GNU Affero General Public License V3
.

• BoppreH指出`or die()`并不是一种好的设计选择，而是一种常见的习惯用法。同时提到类似`file_exists(path)`和`db.query(string)`等函数可能会引发难以调试的竞争条件和SQL注入问题。
• wongarsu则认为PHP的“忽略错误继续运行”的哲学导致了开发者习惯性地使用`or die()`，而在某些情况下，继续运行可能才是正确的行为。并质疑如果编程语言默认会崩溃（如Java的异常机制），开发者是否会更注重错误处理。
• sgtpeppr强调了使正确的事情容易做、错误的事情难以做的重要性，并提到一些开发者习惯于用“这是我们一直以来的做法”来为不好的设计选择辩护，导致问题难以解决。
• hnthrow90348765认为这是一个设计和需求问题，而非语言问题。指出如果没有明确的规划和需求说明，开发者很难考虑到所有可能的错误情况，尤其是在高风险场景下。
• anonzzzies对比了PHP和Node.js中的错误处理，指出`die()`只影响当前请求，而`process.exit()`会退出整个Node服务器。同时提到在实际项目中，常见到不完整的错误处理代码，并建议使用工具检测未处理的情况以提高安全性。
• jauco提供了一个外部资源，Joe Duffy的一篇文章，区分了不同种类的错误以及编程语言应如何处理它们。
• hyperhello指出即便错误处理设计不当，测试不足也是问题，认为至少应该有一次测试能发现失败。
• golergka提到“Pit of Success”（成功之坑）概念，强调设计应使得开发者自然而然地做出正确的选择。

补充讨论：
• 错误处理的设计不仅涉及编程语言的特性，还包括开发者的习惯和项目需求。
• 争议的焦点在于如何在语言设计和开发实践中平衡错误处理的复杂性和实用性。
• 测试和代码审查的重要性在讨论中也被提及，作为发现和纠正错误处理问题的手段。

data.title: Aeron: Efficient reliable UDP unicast, UDP multicast, and IPC message transport
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Aeron是一个高效可靠的 messaging 系统，支持UDP单播、多播以及进程间通信（IPC）。它提供Java、C、C++和.NET客户端，能够在不同机器或同一机器上的进程间高效交换消息。Aeron具备高吞吐量和低延迟特性，集成Simple Binary Encoding (SBE)以提升消息编解码性能。其Archive模块支持将消息流存储到持久存储中，Aeron Cluster则基于Raft算法提供容错服务。Aeron由Adaptive Financial Consulting拥有和运营，提供培训、咨询等服务，并支持一些专有增强功能如内核 bypass 和高速加密。文档和源码可在其GitHub页面和Maven Central获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Aeron的性能和可靠性，以及其使用的UDP和多播技术在实际应用中的表现。

不同观点：
• Veserv认为Aeron的性能并不如宣传的那样高性能。他通过AWS和GCP上的传输协议基准测试数据指出，Aeron在多核心情况下的吞吐量表现不佳，远低于普通的TCP堆栈。他质疑Aeron是否真正达到了高性能的标准，尽管Aeron在延迟和多播支持方面可能有其他优势。

• Vodou基于多年维护使用多播通信的应用套件的经验，对多播的可靠性提出质疑。他认为多播在理论上很好，但在实际应用中由于网络设备和操作系统的问题会带来很多麻烦。他表示不会再在新系统中依赖多播技术。

• Buybackoff认为Aeron的存在本身就是一个重要的贡献，特别是在低延迟系统中。他指出Aeron在单数据中心内的延迟表现优于TCP，尤其是在P99+延迟方面。他还提到Aeron在多播支持上的优势，但也指出在跨数据中心设置中的一些挑战，如缓冲区配置和包丢失问题。

• Neomantra强调Aeron的系统架构和“机械同情”设计理念，认为其高性能不仅仅来自于UDP和多播支持。他详细描述了Aeron的服务器和客户端架构，以及如何通过共享内存队列实现高效的消息传递。

• Arnold_palmur赞赏Aeron代码库的软件质量，认为它是研究软件质量的优秀开源项目，特别是对于Java开发者。

• Readthenotes1对可靠UDP被多次实现的现象表示疑问，暗示可能有重复劳动。

• Fuzzfactor表示喜欢多播的概念，但没有提供具体的使用体验或技术分析。

补充讨论：
• Aeron的性能优势在低延迟和高并发场景下的体现，特别是在单数据中心内，但在跨数据中心时可能不如TCP。
• 多播技术在实际应用中的可靠性问题，特别是在不同网络设备和操作系统上的表现。
• Aeron架构的独特设计及其在共享内存和消息队列方面的创新应用。
• Aeron代码库作为开源项目的质量和学习价值。

争议焦点：
• Aeron在多核心情况下的性能是否真正达到高性能标准，特别是与TCP相比。
• 多播技术的实际可靠性和应用场景的局限性。

Aeron
Efficient reliable UDP unicast, UDP multicast, and IPC message transport. Java, C, and C++ clients are available in this
repository, and a
.NET client
is available. All
clients can exchange messages across machines, or on the same machine via IPC, very efficiently. Message streams can be
recorded by the
Archive
module to persistent storage
for later, or real-time, replay. Aeron
Cluster
provides support for fault-tolerant services as replicated state machines based on the
Raft
consensus algorithm.
Performance is the key focus. A design goal for Aeron is to be the highest throughput with the lowest and most
predictable latency of any messaging system. Aeron integrates with
Simple Binary Encoding (SBE)
for the best possible message
encoding and decoding performance. Many of the data structures used in the creation of Aeron have been factored out to
the
Agrona
project.
For details of usage, protocol specification, FAQ, etc. please check out the
Wiki
.
For the latest version information and changes see the
Change Log
with Java
downloads
at
Maven Central
.
Aeron is owned and operated by Adaptive Financial Consulting. Originally created by Martin Thompson and Todd Montgomery, the Aeron team joined Adaptive in 2022.
For Business users, to get started with Aeron Premium, please visit
Aeron.io
We provide a range of services including:
Training for development and operations with Aeron and Aeron Cluster.
Consulting, for example if you’re not sure how to design your system or need help tuning your system.
We also offer a number of proprietary enhancements on top of Aeron and Aeron Cluster such as kernel bypass (ef_vi, AWS DPDK, and VMA) for increased performance, and blazing fast encryption with ATS.
If you’re building a new trading system, we have experienced Aeron developers who can help.
Please get in touch at
sales@aeron.io
if you would like to learn more about any of these.

data.title: Parse, Don’t Validate – Some C Safety Tips
data.author: lelanthran
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了“解析而非验证”技术在C语言中的应用，以减少可被利用的错误风险。作者指出，常见的验证方法会导致系统深处的代码重复验证输入，增加错误机会。通过在输入边界处直接解析输入数据为特定类型（如`email_t`），可以避免系统内部重复验证的问题。文章建议使用不透明类型来替代`char *`，确保数据类型安全，防止恶意输入。这种方法不仅提高了安全性，还能借助编译器类型检查进一步减少攻击面。最终，只有边界处的函数处理原始`char *`输入，内部函数只接受已验证的类型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过解析输入并利用类型系统进行验证的编程实践

不同观点：
• [myaccountonhn] 认为在"边缘"将输入解析为适合问题域的数据结构是好的做法，可以提高代码的可维护性。然而，过度使用 newtype 包装会增加不必要的仪式性和样板代码。如果数据可以合理地表示为原始类型，则应直接使用原始类型。此外，与大量使用 newtype 的库交互可能会导致问题，尤其是当库没有提供访问内部数据的途径时。
• [OptionOfT] 支持充分利用类型系统来防止错误。通过使用特定类型（如 ValidatedEmail、PriviligedUser）可以让编译器提供保护，减少代码中的条件检查，提高代码的安全性和可读性。
• [o11c] 指出不应在自定义类型中使用 "_t" 后缀，因为这是为未来标准类型保留的。同时，认为防止双重释放的声明是无效的，C 语言在对象所有权方面表现不佳。
• [hackrmn] 强调通过解析输入和利用类型系统来提高代码的健壮性，但指出在实践中往往难以说服同事采用这种方法。许多开发者仍然依赖于分散的验证函数，而没有充分利用类型系统。
• [hansvm] 提到 "Parse, Don't Validate" 方法在实际代码库中可能导致类型的组合爆炸。如果需要同时满足多个条件，可能导致中间类型和解析代码的指数增长。提出了一种使用编译时标记来解决此问题的方案。
• [pianoben] 认为虽然概念上同意这种方法，但在实际操作中处理解析结果非常困难，尤其是当需要将自定义类型转换回基本类型时。
• [rorylaitila] 分享了自己在 web 应用中使用这种方法的经验，通过自动生成值对象和访问器类来解决大量字段的验证问题，但指出这种方法可能在性能上有所影响。
• [anon-3988] 强调在 C 语言中实现安全性需要使用 newtype 模式，将信息封装在结构体中，并建议在创建和消费时以外部库处理指针。
• [charcircuit] 简单表示不信任 C 开发者处理字符串的能力。
• [belter] 认为 "Parse, Don't Validate" 模式只是防御的一部分，还需要结合资源限制和其他保护措施。

补充讨论：
• 关于使用 "_t" 后缀的争议，多个评论指出这是保留给标准类型的，自定义类型不应使用。
• 讨论中多次提到性能问题，特别是在 web 应用中处理大量数据时的性能影响。
• 对于 C 语言中的安全性和内存管理问题，有评论指出需要更好的所有权管理和防止双重释放的措施。
• 关于说服其他开发者采用这种方法的困难，强调了实际应用中的文化和沟通挑战。

争议的焦点：
• 使用 newtype 模式的必要性和其带来的仪式性代码的权衡。
• 在实际项目中应用 "Parse, Don't Validate" 模式的可行性和复杂性。
• 在 C 语言中处理字符串和内存管理的固有困难和风险。

44507405.article_content:
âA good programmer is someone who looks both ways before crossing a one-way street.â â Doug Linder
previous:
Contents
Posted by Lelanthran
2025-03-27
âParse, Donât Validateâ
- the long version
If youâve read the original post on
âParse, Donât Validateâ
you may have noticed that it focuses primarily on conceptual correctness. Here, Iâll build on that by showing how this technique can be used outside of niche academic languages by demonstrating it in a language that is as practical as it is dangerous - C.
In this blog post you will see three techniques of reducing the risk of exploitable errors in C.
âParse, Donât Validateâ
- the TLDR version
The basic idea is this:
Data Comes Into Your System.
Your System Processes It.
Your first instinct, when your system receives as input an email address (for example), is to perform
validateEmail(untrustedInput)
and then pass the validated string further into the depths of the system for usage.
The problem is that other code deep within the rest of the system is going to
also
do some sort of validation on the string they just got. Every single function deep within the bowels of the system will
still
need to validate the input before processing it.
Iâll bet good money that the processing functions will attempt to validate their input. Because theyâre logically far away from the boundary, theyâll either do it a different way or fail to do it altogether.
So instead of this:
// Pseudocode
if
(validateEmail(untrustedInput) != true) {
return
error;
}
// Rest of system uses `untrustedInput`
Rather do this instead:
// Pseudocode
email_t theEmail = parseEmail(untrustedInput);
if
(theEmail == PARSE_ERROR) {
return
error;
}
// Rest of system uses `theEmail`
This removes any opportunity for errors to creep in within the rest of the system, such as some other code using a different
validateEmail
function on the
untrustedInput
, for example.
Some conventions for Safety in C.
What does this have to do with C strings? Good question.
Much to the surprise of, well, everybody, C
actually has
type safety. Sure, it isnât as enforceable as (for example) Rustâ¦ and, sure, if you are willing to do extra work you can bypass it, but, at the end of the day, the compiler
will still warn you
if you try to add a number to a string and assign the result to a function.
With some exceptions, when you mismatch types, the compiler
will
tell you about it.
The problem isnât that C lacks type safety (it clearly enforces most types in most expressions), itâs that raw pointers do not encode semantics (e.g., a
char *
doesnât tell you if itâs an email, a name, or a filename).
This is pretty much the same in every language; if you have a function
store_user()
which accepts two strings, an email and a user name, then no type safety in the world is going to save you if you accidentally swap the arguments around when calling the function.
But, you still have options â even in C â by creating new string types; one for email and another for user name.
When writing in C, instead of passing
char *
around as strings, or (safer, but not by much) using an existing string library that stores length + bufferâ¦ rather create an opaque type for it.
You parse the input into the correct type
once
, and then functions which accept that type will produce a compile error if you mix things up.
To create opaque types,
read this post
.
When you create the correct types for
data entering the system
, you can then do this:
// C code, not pseudocode
email_t *email = parse_email(untrusted_input);
if
(!email) {
// Handle error
}
In addition to the safey from using opaque types thereâs even more levels of safety here too, starting with:
You remove all occurrences of
char *
values in your system. You force the only occurrences of
char *
values to be at the boundary of your system, where
all input is untrusted anyway!
This is not only for
char *
types though; you can do it to
all
values entering your system.You parse them once into the correct data type, and then code deep in the belly of the system
cannot
be compromised with malicious input, because the
only
data that the rest of the system will see is data that has been parsed into specific types.
When your functions never accept
char *
parameters your risk of pwnage is reduced. By leveraging the typing guarantees in C, you can ensure that the system wonât compile
even if
some heretic decides that they want to pass a
char *
to a function expecting an
email_t
.
Only the functions on the boundary of the system, interfacing to the outside world, should parse input. Everything else should accept
only
type-checkable parameters.
That alone is a big reason to use this approach, but Iâll point out two more opportunities to reduce the attack surface of your system using an actual compilable example consisting of separate compilation units. The untrusted input
email
and
name
come from outside the system.
First, the header declaring your custom ty
44507405.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了“解析而非验证”技术在C语言中的应用，以减少可被利用的错误风险。作者指出，常见的验证方法会导致系统深处的代码重复验证输入，增加错误机会。通过在输入边界处直接解析输入数据为特定类型（如`email_t`），可以避免系统内部重复验证的问题。文章建议使用不透明类型来替代`char *`，确保数据类型安全，防止恶意输入。这种方法不仅提高了安全性，还能借助编译器类型检查进一步减少攻击面。最终，只有边界处的函数处理原始`char *`输入，内部函数只接受已验证的类型。
44507405.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过解析输入并利用类型系统进行验证的编程实践

不同观点：
• [myaccountonhn] 认为在"边缘"将输入解析为适合问题域的数据结构是好的做法，可以提高代码的可维护性。然而，过度使用 newtype 包装会增加不必要的仪式性和样板代码。如果数据可以合理地表示为原始类型，则应直接使用原始类型。此外，与大量使用 newtype 的库交互可能会导致问题，尤其是当库没有提供访问内部数据的途径时。
• [OptionOfT] 支持充分利用类型系统来防止错误。通过使用特定类型（如 ValidatedEmail、PriviligedUser）可以让编译器提供保护，减少代码中的条件检查，提高代码的安全性和可读性。
• [o11c] 指出不应在自定义类型中使用 "_t" 后缀，因为这是为未来标准类型保留的。同时，认为防止双重释放的声明是无效的，C 语言在对象所有权方面表现不佳。
• [hackrmn] 强调通过解析输入和利用类型系统来提高代码的健壮性，但指出在实践中往往难以说服同事采用这种方法。许多开发者仍然依赖于分散的验证函数，而没有充分利用类型系统。
• [hansvm] 提到 "Parse, Don't Validate" 方法在实际代码库中可能导致类型的组合爆炸。如果需要同时满足多个条件，可能导致中间类型和解析代码的指数增长。提出了一种使用编译时标记来解决此问题的方案。
• [pianoben] 认为虽然概念上同意这种方法，但在实际操作中处理解析结果非常困难，尤其是当需要将自定义类型转换回基本类型时。
• [rorylaitila] 分享了自己在 web 应用中使用这种方法的经验，通过自动生成值对象和访问器类来解决大量字段的验证问题，但指出这种方法可能在性能上有所影响。
• [anon-3988] 强调在 C 语言中实现安全性需要使用 newtype 模式，将信息封装在结构体中，并建议在创建和消费时以外部库处理指针。
• [charcircuit] 简单表示不信任 C 开发者处理字符串的能力。
• [belter] 认为 "Parse, Don't Validate" 模式只是防御的一部分，还需要结合资源限制和其他保护措施。

补充讨论：
• 关于使用 "_t" 后缀的争议，多个评论指出这是保留给标准类型的，自定义类型不应使用。
• 讨论中多次提到性能问题，特别是在 web 应用中处理大量数据时的性能影响。
• 对于 C 语言中的安全性和内存管理问题，有评论指出需要更好的所有权管理和防止双重释放的措施。
• 关于说服其他开发者采用这种方法的困难，强调了实际应用中的文化和沟通挑战。

争议的焦点：
• 使用 newtype 模式的必要性和其带来的仪式性代码的权衡。
• 在实际项目中应用 "Parse, Don't Validate" 模式的可行性和复杂性。
• 在 C 语言中处理字符串和内存管理的固有困难和风险。

data.title: New Windows 11 build adds self-healing "quick machine recovery" feature
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 微软正在为Windows 11添加一项名为快速机器恢复（QMR）的新功能，以帮助修复崩溃的电脑。QMR允许电脑启动进入Windows恢复环境（WinRE），连接互联网并下载微软提供的修复程序，解决可能导致电脑无法正常启动的问题。这一技术是微软"Windows弹性计划"的一部分，旨在避免类似2024年中CrowdStrike安全产品更新导致的大规模Windows电脑故障。QMR最初在Windows Insider项目的Canary通道中推出，并可能逐步推广到更广泛的用户群。此外，微软还在准备Windows 11 25H2年度更新，其中一些功能将预先安装但暂时禁用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 11操作系统的问题与新功能（自修复工具）的讨论

不同观点：
• [anon7000]: 认为Win11是最近几年用过的最不可靠的操作系统，存在卡顿、蓝屏、设备兼容性问题（如音频接口）等，对新推出的自修复工具持怀疑态度，认为Windows的故障排查机制不够透明，且修复工具可能无效。
• [ChocolateGod]: 对微软放弃Windows 10X表示遗憾，认为其可以解决系统升级导致的致命问题，而现在则是在用“权宜之计”应对糟糕的系统设计，类似于Android的更新机制。
• [ksec]: 对Win11的总体评价较为正面，认为虽然仍有一些小问题（如广告和UI），但相比Win10有所改进。希望微软能够更快速地迭代版本，并认为Windows仍有改进空间。
• [potato-peeler]: 对微软Canary测试通道的命名习惯提出质疑，指出与公司内部使用的定义不一致，Canary在其公司是介于开发和测试之间的阶段。
• [instagib]: 提到最近的一次更新导致硬盘无法启动或挂载，新的Win11安装缺少恢复模式，需要手动修复，对系统的稳定性表示担忧。
• [bni]: 批评Windows UI越来越破碎和臃肿，希望微软能够首先解决这些问题。
• [userbinator]: 对“自修复”功能持讽刺态度，认为这实际上是微软强制撤销用户所做的某些更改。
• [kitsune_]: 希望新功能能够支持旧硬件（如6700k处理器）。
• [PUSH_AX]: 简单批评微软在“粉饰糟粕”，暗示新功能只是表面功夫。
• [hulitu]: 怀疑新功能会在未来的更新中被破坏，遵循微软传统，新功能可能带来新的问题。
• [anthk]: 提到Fedora Silverblue等基于OSTree的Linux发行版早已具备自修复和回滚功能，暗示微软在这方面落后于Linux社区。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Windows 11的稳定性和新功能是否能真正解决问题。许多用户对系统的可靠性表示不满，并对微软的故障排查和修复机制持怀疑态度。
• 一些用户对微软的开发和测试通道命名习惯提出质疑，显示出对微软内部开发流程的不满或误解。
• 有用户提到Linux发行版在自修复和系统回滚方面的先进性，暗示微软可能在某些技术上落后于开源社区。

总结：用户对Windows 11的可靠性和新功能持不同看法，一些人对其表示强烈不满，认为新功能可能只是权宜之计，而另一些人则认为系统在逐步改进，但仍有很大提升空间。争议的焦点在于系统的稳定性、硬件兼容性和故障排查机制的有效性。

Microsoft is adding a new recovery mode to Windows to help revive crashing PCs. Called quick machine recovery (QMR), this technology enables Windows 11 PCs to boot into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE, also used by Windows install media and IT shops for various recovery and diagnostic purposes), connect to the Internet, and download Microsoft-provided fixes for "widespread boot issues" that could be keeping the PC from booting properly.
Initially
announced in late 2024
as part of the "Windows Resiliency Initiative," QMR is one of a couple of steps that Microsoft is taking
to prevent a repeat of mid-2024's CrowdStrike outage
, when a bugged update to one of CrowdStrike's security products brought down millions of Windows PCs and servers and caused widespread service outages in many industries. Fixing some of those PCs required booting and fixing each one individually; QMR should make it possible to apply that kind of fix remotely even if a PC is so broken that it can't boot into Windows proper.
The initial version of the QMR feature is
rolling out to Windows 11 PCs
enrolled in the Canary channel of Microsoft's Windows Insider testing program. This is the least stable and most experimental of the four Windows 11 testing channels. As Microsoft adds features and fixes bugs, it should gradually move to the Dev, Beta, and Release Preview channels before rolling out to the Windows user base more broadly.
Preview build 27898 also includes a features that will shrink Taskbar items if you've got too many pins or running apps for everything to fit at once, changes the pop-up that apps use to ask for access to things like the system webcam or microphone, and allows you to add words to the dictionary used for the speech-to-text voice access features, among a handful of other changes.
It's hard to predict when any given Windows Insider feature will roll out to the regular non-preview versions of Windows, but we're likely just a few months out from the launch of Windows 11 25H2, this year's "annual feature update." Some of these updates, like last year's 24H2, are fairly major overhauls that make lots of under-the-hood changes. Others, like 2023's 23H2, mostly exist to change the version number and reset Microsoft's security update clock, as each yearly update is only promised new security updates
for two years after release
.
The 25H2 update looks like one of the relatively minor ones. Microsoft
says
that the two versions "use a shared servicing branch," and that 25H2 features will be "staged" on PCs running Windows 11 24H2, meaning that the code will be installed on systems via Windows Update but that they'll be disabled initially. Installing the 25H2 "update" when it's available will merely enable features that were installed but dormant.

data.title: Ask HN: Where are the AI-driven profits or promotions?
data.author: arduinomancer
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对生产力、工资和企业竞争的影响

不同观点：
• **[aisikaakaccc]**：AI工具提高了开发者的生产力，但产生了一些质量问题。举例说明了高级开发者和低绩效开发者如何使用AI工具，前者虽然产出更多，但质量不佳，而后者则让代码审查过程更加耗时。他认为AI工具在实际使用中并没有网上声称的那么神奇，只有在特定场景（如翻译）中才能显著提高生产力。

• **[jostylr]**：AI带来的生产力提升可能会通过市场竞争影响工资和利润。如果工人能够利用AI工具提高自身竞争力并跳槽到更高薪的岗位，他们的工资可能会提高。此外，企业可以通过降低成本和提高效率来增加利润。最终，AI工具可能会催生更多独立项目和创业机会。

• **[matt_s]**：工人不会从生产力提升中直接受益，因为利润主要流向企业主和管理层。即使AI工具提高了工人的生产力，工人也很难获得相应的工资增长。工人要获得更多收益，可能需要自己创业，但这比单纯编写软件要复杂得多。

• **[grafmax]**：生产力提升通常不会自动转化为工人工资的增加，因为企业主不会主动分享利润，除非受到外部压力。历史数据显示，自1980年以来，生产力与工资之间的差距越来越大，工人的生产力收益大部分流向了富裕阶层。要改变这种情况，可能需要通过工会化等手段对企业主施加压力。

• **[muzani]**：AI工具显著降低了创业和开发的风险与成本，例如快速构建原型和减少技术债务。尽管存在一些失败案例，但总体上AI工具提高了生产力和创业成功率。

• **[molteanu]**：在其公司中，尽管广泛使用AI工具，但并未显著提升开发速度或激发更多创意。AI工具的引入更像是一个没有明确指导的开放选择，缺乏对好坏的判断。

• **[AznHisoka]**：如果所有人都能使用相同的AI工具，那么个别工程师很难通过这些工具获得超常的职业发展或财富积累，因为大家的生产力都得到了提升。

• **[gavinray]**：有些公司正在尝试通过量化和补偿提高生产力的员工来留住他们。虽然这种方法不一定适用于所有组织，但在某些情况下是可行的。

• **[francisofascii]**：AI工具的普及可能导致工程师供过于求，从而降低他们的市场工资。例如，微软的股票价格上涨并没有直接提高工程师的工资。

• **[i_have_an_idea]**：AI工具在特定情况下非常有用，例如挽救和管理不善的外包项目，避免公司遭受重大损失。

• **[mojomark]**：尽管个人日常使用ChatGPT提高效率，但这些提升并未被广泛认可或转化为实际利润。

data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何拍摄国际空间站（ISS）凌日画面。首先，利用transit-finder.com网站查询附近凌日信息，并提前规划行程和设备。推荐使用至少800mm焦距的相机，太阳凌日需加装太阳滤镜，三脚架和遥控快门必备。提前一天踩点并提早到达拍摄地点，检查设备和路径。拍摄时使用RAW格式和连续拍摄模式，ISO尽量低，曝光时间不超过1毫秒。由于凌日时间极短且可能有误差，建议提前5-10秒开始拍摄，并持续至少10秒。最后，检查照片确认是否捕捉到ISS。

ENTER YOUR EMAIL HERE FOR MY TELESCOPE BUYING GUIDE
My ISS transit shots tend to get the most questions, so I put together a write-up  of exactly how I get them.
See the uncropped version of my latest ISS Transit shot here
(you can order print there as well, get some cool space art while supporting my projects)
First- I check
transit-finder.com
.
This is a web resource that allows you to put in your location, a time frame, and how far you're willing to drive, and it will spit out results of nearby transits. I check this every week, and see my transits coming about a month ahead of time. The results can change though based on updated ISS trajectories though, so check it often. The results generally look like this:
This gives me information about the upcoming transits, so I'll know how good they are. The arrow shows path of travel from your current location, but if you travel the distance indicated towards the path of the transit you will be able to capture it. Many of the results will be far too small to resolve details on the ISS, so I generally skip those ones. "ISS angular size" is one of the only details that matters. I generally only shoot ones that are over 45", but some photographers have captured great ones that are smaller. If it is nearly straight overhead, it is larger since that is when it is closest. That second transit in that image is the best one, but it is also fairly far away at 31km. Still though, 62" (that's arcseconds) is about as "big" as the Iss gets for these, I've only seen a couple larger than that.
Next, I would plan the gear for my shot.
I am lucky to have a lot of good equipment at my fingertips, but really you just need a camera with a fairly long focal length. I recommend at least 800mm, but the more the better (so long as your f# doesn't get so high you have to increase exposure time).  I have actually captured transits with a 350mm lens where I was still able to resolve the  solar panels, so don't let your lack of equipment necessarily deter you! If it's a solar transit, you can get solar filters for cheap that block enough light to safely shoot the transit. It won't show solar atmospheric details like my solar scope, but it'll be good enough to see the clear silhouette. A tracking mount helps you keep it in frame, but since the transit itself is so short it is technically unnecessary. A remote shutter/intervalometer is highly recommended. Definitely use a tripod.
Then- scout the location.
If you are travelling to the shooting location, make sure there is a public spot with enough room to set up your camera. I generally do this the day before the transit so I can check the site again and make sure the ISS didn't change positions.
Set up early
I generally show up at least an hour early to these, sometimes several hours early. This gives me time to double check the ISS hasn't changed paths (again, via
transit-finder.com
) and test my equipment.
Prepping for the shot
Once I have my gear set up and pointed at the moon/sun (with appropriate filters) I test my equipment. These transits are always less than a second, so making sure the camera is able to take frames as quickly as possible ensures you are ready when the time comes. Also, take this time to focus on the subject, and take test frames. Always shoot with the lowest ISO/Gain possible, but keep exposure length at no longer than 1ms or 1/1000s. Any longer and the ISS starts to show motion blur. Make sure you're on a continuous shooting mode in RAW. Take test shots to see how fast your camera can shoot, for about 20 seconds. (Note- having a memory card with the fastest write speed is paramount here) Have a clock with seconds counting visible. I use my laptop with
time.gov
running so I know the time is accurate to the millisecond. Frame your target with enough margin for error that if the ISS passes above or below the expected trajectory it is still in frame. I find it is generally within a few arc minutes of the expected path, but have seen many that missed by up to 10 arc minutes (1/6 a degree, or about a third the width of the moon/sun).
Start shooting Early, and Keep shooting after the pass
You probably won't actually see the pass, unless you have a laptop showing a live view through the lens. You'll just have to trust your clock and the pass information to know it happened. For this reason, I always start shooting 5-10 seconds early, and keep shooting for at least 10 seconds after the event. The ISS is almost never exactly on time based on my information, so this allows you some margin of error. If your camera does not record shots quickly enough, I would recommend doing this with a high resolution video instead.
Check your frames to see if you caught it!
