• [ygritte] 对某些评论中提到的社会契约和规则崩溃持怀疑态度，认为这些规则从未真正存在过。
• [danieltanfh95] 认为人才争夺战是被资本推动的泡沫，资本并没有真正找到最有潜力的创新者，而是过度集中于少数人身上，导致资本分配效率低下。
• [torginus] 认为当前的资本争夺只是资本主义竞争的常态，通过高薪聘请顶尖人才并最终出售公司或技术是常见的商业策略。
• [zer00eyz] 认为当前的AI泡沫已经达到顶峰，顶级公司和高薪聘请并不能保证真正的创新，真正的突破可能来自未来的经济萧条和新的基础技术发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于当前AI资本 influx 是否合理及其对社会和行业的长远影响。
• 人才争夺战中的高薪和高估值是否真实反映了人才的价值，还是只是资本泡沫的一部分。
• 资本是否应该更广泛地投资于基础技术和多样化人才，以寻找新的创新点。
• 当前的资本集中和不平等是否会导致社会问题，如员工被忽视和裁员潮。

data.title: Black hole merger challenges our understanding of black hole formation
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 2023年11月23日，LIGO合作组织宣布探测到迄今为止最大的黑洞合并事件，产生了一个质量超过太阳225倍的巨型黑洞。该信号名为GW231123，涉及两个质量分别为太阳137倍和103倍的黑洞，其合并产生了强烈的引力波，被LIGO探测到。这一事件挑战了现有的恒星演化模型，因为根据标准模型，如此大规模的黑洞合并是不太可能的。科学家推测，这些黑洞可能通过 earlier 的黑洞合并形成。此次探测不仅标志着引力波天文学的重大突破，也提出了关于黑洞形成的新问题。研究结果将在即将召开的国际会议上公布，整个科学界将进一步分析这一复杂信号。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：黑洞碰撞事件及其对当前天文学理解的挑战

不同观点：
• Roark66质疑黑洞如何能够真正碰撞，基于时间在接近黑洞奇点时会变慢的理论，认为从外部观察者角度看，黑洞似乎永远不会真正碰撞。他提出，如果碰撞被视为进入彼此事件视界内，那么观察到的这些事件是否意味着宇宙年龄是无限的。
• VagabundoP对黑洞的质量感到困惑，指出这些黑洞的质量处于“ forbidden zone”（禁止区），即根据形成方式，它们的质量不应存在。他猜测这些黑洞可能是第二或第三代黑洞，但认为在如此近的距离形成是不太可能的。
• misja111不理解为什么225太阳质量的合并被认为不应该存在，因为已有理论表明存在数百万太阳质量的黑洞，它们通过多次合并形成。
• gmuslera通过科幻小说引喻，强调两次大规模黑洞合并可能对附近星系造成巨大影响。
• Stevemiller07对LIGO和Virgo的发现表示赞叹，认为每次新事件都带来更多疑问。
• ErigmolCt对225太阳质量的黑洞合并感到惊讶，指出尽管建立了模型预测这些事件不应该发生，但宇宙现象常常打破这些模型。
• debugnik质疑文章未能解释为什么这次事件挑战了我们对黑洞的理解，并希望知道是否因为预期大质量物体应螺旋更久。
• thaumasiotes关注质量守恒问题，质疑合并后质量如何变化，并提出几种可能的解释，如质量转化为能量或物质逃逸事件视界。
• ReptileMan总结宇宙比想象的更复杂，即使从已经认为很复杂的立场出发。
• gnabgib批评文章标题具有点击诱饵性质，认为它没有准确反映科学发现。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中反复提到黑洞质量和合并事件的不确定性，以及当前天文学模型在解释这些现象时的局限性。
• 参与者普遍对新发现感到兴奋和困惑，反映出科学发现不断推动理论边界的本质。
• 对媒体报道和科学传播方式的批评，指出点击诱饵标题对科学讨论无益。

Artist's interpretation of a black hole merger.
Credit: Caltech-LIGO
Gravitational waves
âripples in space-time caused by violent cosmic eventsâtravel at the speed of light in every direction, eventually fading out like ripples in water. But some events are so destructive and extreme that they create disturbances in spacetime more like powerful waves than small ripples, with enough energy to reach our own detectors here on Earth.Â
Today, the LIGO Collaboration announced the detection of the most colossal black hole merger known to date, the final product of which appears to be a gigantic black hole more than 225 times the mass of the Sun. Much about this signal, designated GW231123, contradicts known models for stellar evolution, sending physicists scrambling to apprehend how such a merger was even possible.
LIGO, or
the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory
, made physics history in 2015 by
detecting gravitational waves for the first time
, capturing the cosmological echo of two colliding black holes. Since its Nobel-winning discovery, the
LIGO Collaboration
, an international partnership between LIGO and Virgo and KAGRA in Italy and Japan, respectively, has continued its meticulous surveillance of the galaxy. The collaboration has detected numerous signals from neutron stars, supernovas, and some 300 black hole mergers.
The LIGO Laboratory operates two detector sites, one near Hanford in eastern Washington, and another near Livingston, Louisiana. This photo shows the Livingston detector site. Credit: Caltech/MIT/LIGO Lab
But GW231123, first observed on November 23, 2023, seems to be an unprecedented beast of a black hole merger. Two enormous black holesâ137 and 103 times the mass of the Sunâmanaged to keep it together despite their immense combined mass, spinning at 400,000 times the speed of Earth’s rotation to form an ever bigger black hole.
To put its size into perspective, the previous record holder for such a merger,Â
GW190521
, is roughly 140 times the mass of the Sun.
âThis is the most massive black hole binary weâve observed through gravitational waves, and it presents a real challenge to our understanding of black hole formation.â
Considering the gravitationally chaotic nature of black hole environments, with their pushes and pulls, it’s remarkable that this merger was stable enough for the resulting gravitational waves to reach LIGO, which detected the signals for a duration of 0.1 seconds. Such episodes should be âforbiddenâ according to standard evolution models, said Mark Hannam, LIGO member and physicist at Cardiff University, in a
statement
.Â
âOne possibility is that the two black holes in this binary formed through earlier mergers of smaller black holes,â he surmised. âThis is the most massive black hole binary weâve observed through gravitational waves, and it presents a real challenge to our understanding of black hole formation.â
Infographic on the binary black hole merger that produced the GW231123 signal. Credit: Simona J. Miller/Caltech
âThe black holes appear to be spinning very rapidlyânear the limit allowed by Einsteinâs theory of general relativity,â explained Charlie Hoy, LIGO member and physicist at the University of Portsmouth in England, in the same release. âThat makes the signal difficult to model and interpret. Itâs an excellent case study for pushing forward the development of our theoretical tools.â
Scientists will present their findings aboutÂ GW231123 next week at the 24th International Conference on General Relativity and Gravitation (GR24) and the 16th Edoardo Amaldi Conference on Gravitational Waves, held jointly as the GR-Amaldi meeting in Glasgow, U.K. Following that, the data will be out for public scrutiny, kicking off the race to unravel GW231123âs mysteryâthough itâs unlikely weâll have a clear answer any time soon.
“It will take years for the community to fully unravel this intricate signal pattern and all its implications,” added Gregorio Carullo, also a LIGO member and physicist at the University of Birmingham, England. “Despite the most likely explanation remaining a black hole merger, more complex scenarios could be the key to deciphering its unexpected features. Exciting times ahead!”
Physicists first conceived of gravitational waves as early as the late 19th century, but the idea gained popular momentum thanks to Albert Einstein. As one of the few observational methods that doesnât need light to âseeâ cosmic phenomena, gravitational waves are unmatched in their potential for helping humanity uncover the many mysteries of
black holes
,
ancient stars
, and even
dark matter
. So, indeedâexciting times ahead!

data.title: Investors bought 27% of US homes in Q1, as traditional buyers struggle to afford
data.author: MilnerRoute
data.article_summary: 美国房地产投资者正购买更大比例的房屋，因高房价和借贷成本上升使传统买家望而却步。根据房地产数据公司BatchData的报告，2025年第一季度近27%的房屋由投资者购买，为至少五年来最高比例。2020至2023年间，投资者购房比例平均为18.5%。尽管整体销售增长 modest，投资者购房比例上升反映出住房市场放缓，传统买家面临更大的负担能力限制。自2022年初以来，由于抵押贷款利率上升，美国住房市场陷入销售低迷，去年房屋销售达到近30年最低。今年市场依然疲软，许多潜在买家因高利率和不断上涨的房价却步。随着房屋销售放缓，房产待售时间变长，库存增加，这使能够现金支付或利用房屋净值收益的投资者受益。尽管如此，投资者拥有的房屋约占全美8600万套独立屋的20%，其中小型投资者（拥有1至5套房屋）占85%。大型机构投资者（拥有1000套以上房屋）仅占约2.2%，且有缩减趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：房地产投资对住房市场的影响以及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• **关注机构投资者的影响**：mattmcknight指出，文章末尾提到机构投资者正在减少购房，这与许多评论的观点相矛盾。文章数据显示，拥有1000套或更多房屋的机构投资者仅占所有投资房的比例为2.2%，且有迹象表明这些大投资者正在减少购房。

• **住房市场结构性问题**：cglan认为当前的住房市场反映了长期存在的结构性问题，即住房供应不足导致房价上涨，使得只有投资者或资产较多的人能够进入市场。现有的杠杆、30年期抵押贷款和税收减免政策继续补贴现有的房主，而牺牲无房者的利益。

• **不同类型投资者的区别**：bradly强调，拥有1到5套房的个人投资者占85%，而机构投资者仅占2.2%，这两类投资者的动机和操作方式不同，可能需要不同的监管方式。

• **现金购房的影响**：ChrisMarshallNY分享了其朋友所在公司通过现金购买房屋进行翻新出租的实例，指出这种做法在当前高利率环境下给普通购房者带来了竞争压力。

• **创新住房解决方案**：bee_rider提议开发一种可大规模生产的RV（房车），以适应年轻一代的需求，并提出这种住房方式可以避免传统房屋的弊端，尤其在气候变化背景下。

44554713.article_content:
Investors snap up growing share of US homes as traditional buyers struggle to afford one
Real estate investors are buying a larger share of U.S. homes as high prices and borrowing costs deter traditional buyers
By
ALEX VEIGA AP business writer
July 7, 2025, 1:10 PM
1:32
FILE - A home for sale in Sudbury, Mass., is shown on Sunday, Sept. 22, 2024. (AP Photo/Peter Morgan, File)
The Associated Press
LOS ANGELES --
Real estate investors are snapping up a bigger share of U.S. homes on the market as rising prices and stubbornly high borrowing costs freeze out many other would-be homebuyers.
Nearly 27% of all homes sold in the first three months of the year were bought by investors -- the highest share in at least five years, according to a report by real estate data provider BatchData.
Between 2020 and 2023, the share of homes bought by investors averaged 18.5%.
All told, investors bought 265,000 homes in the January-March quarter, an increase of 1.2% from the same period a year earlier, the firm said.
Despite the modest annual increase, the rise in the share of investor home purchases is more a reflection of how much the housing market has slowed as traditional buyers face growing affordability constraints, according to BatchData.
The U.S. housing market has been in a sales slump since early 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows. Home sales fell last year to their lowest level
in nearly 30 years.
They’ve remained sluggish
so far this year, as many prospective homebuyers have been discouraged by
elevated mortgage rates
and home prices that have kept climbing, though more slowly.
As home sales have slowed, properties are taking longer to sell. That's led to a sharply higher inventory of homes on the market, benefitting investors and other home shoppers who can afford to bypass current mortgage rates by paying in cash or tapping home equity gains.
“As traditional buyers struggle with affordability, investors with cash and financing advantages are stepping in to maintain transaction volume,” according to the report.
BatchData analyzes U.S. home sales records to determine which properties were purchased by investors. These could include vacation homes or rentals, but not a homebuyer’s primary residence.
Investors bought 1.2 million homes in 2024, up from an average of 1.1 million homes a year going back to 2020, according to BatchData.
Even so, investor-owned homes account for roughly 20% of the nation's 86 million single-family homes, the firm said.
Of those, mom-and-pop investors, or those who own between 1 and 5 homes, account for 85% of all investor-owned residential properties, while those with between 6 and 10 properties account for another 5%.
Institutional investors that own 1,000 or more homes account for only about 2.2% of all investor-owned homes, the firm said.
And that number could get smaller, amid signs that large institutional investors are scaling back home purchases.
Out of a group of eight of the biggest companies that own and lease single-family houses, including Invitation Homes and American Homes 4 Rent, six sold more homes in the second quarter than they bought, according to data from Parcl Labs.

44554713.article_summary: 美国房地产投资者正购买更大比例的房屋，因高房价和借贷成本上升使传统买家望而却步。根据房地产数据公司BatchData的报告，2025年第一季度近27%的房屋由投资者购买，为至少五年来最高比例。2020至2023年间，投资者购房比例平均为18.5%。尽管整体销售增长 modest，投资者购房比例上升反映出住房市场放缓，传统买家面临更大的负担能力限制。自2022年初以来，由于抵押贷款利率上升，美国住房市场陷入销售低迷，去年房屋销售达到近30年最低。今年市场依然疲软，许多潜在买家因高利率和不断上涨的房价却步。随着房屋销售放缓，房产待售时间变长，库存增加，这使能够现金支付或利用房屋净值收益的投资者受益。尽管如此，投资者拥有的房屋约占全美8600万套独立屋的20%，其中小型投资者（拥有1至5套房屋）占85%。大型机构投资者（拥有1000套以上房屋）仅占约2.2%，且有缩减趋势。

data.title: Ask HN: How much of OpenAI code is written by AI?
data.author: growbell_social
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件工程中的作用及其对人类工程师的影响

不同观点：
• Charlesju认为，AI确实推动了大量代码的生成，但几乎所有高速度的生产代码仍然需要人类软件工程师的监督。他强调，AI只是帮助人类更快地构建软件的工具之一，而不是完全取代人类。他还指出，历史上编程一直受到各种工具的辅助，AI只是这一趋势的延续。

• Notfried分享了Anthropic CPO的观点，指出AI可能已经编写了其项目中95%以上的代码，显示出AI在某些公司中的高度应用。

• Crop_rotation和AppreciatorBus指出，自动化趋势通常由相关专业人士推动，即使这意味着他们的工作可能被自动化取代。他们提到，软件工程师长期以来也在自动化其他职业的工作，因此如果他们的工作被自动化，也是一种历史的轮回。

• Ianpurton实际使用Codex的体验显示，他90%的PR（拉取请求）是由AI生成的，人类在循环中进行监督和审查。他强调AI提高了生产力，使他能同时处理多个任务。

• YZF认为，尽管AI在编写代码方面有所改进，但它仍然需要人类的指导和审查。AI在某些领域表现更好，但在其他领域则不然。他提到，随着软件组织变得更大，AI可能帮助减少团队规模和浪费，但整体影响是复杂的，涉及多种因素。

• Ivraatiems相信，AI生成的代码在一定程度上广泛存在，但并不意味着人类工程师的作用会被完全取代。高质量的工程师在监督和提示AI生成代码方面仍然非常有价值，AI工具目前还不完全可靠，需要人类工程师的智慧来使用。

• Crazylogger用编译器的类比说明，AI和人类工程师在不同层次上工作，编译器生成代码的同时，人类设计和构建软件架构。

• Theusus根据个人经验指出，他需要审查大量AI编写的代码，有时还需要自己编写代码，因为AI并不总是能正确理解需求。

• Welder建议使用Wakatime等插件来准确跟踪AI生成的代码与人类编写的代码的比例，以获得更精确的估计。

• Add-sub-mul-div提到，员工希望减少工作量，而雇主希望减少员工数量，AI在这两者之间创造了强大的共生关系，双方都在短期内获利。

补充讨论：
• AI是否会取代人类工程师的角色存在争议。一些评论者认为AI只是工具，人类工程师仍然不可或缺，而另一些评论者则指出AI的高度应用可能导致某些角色被自动化取代。
• AI在不同领域和任务中的表现不同，有些领域AI表现更好，而其他领域则仍然需要人类工程师的深度参与。
• 自动化和AI工具的引入提高了生产力，但也带来了对未来工作岗位和职业发展的担忧。

data.title: Dogwalk: Blender Studio's Official Game
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 《DOGWALK》是由Blender Studio开发和发布的一款免费、开源的休闲游戏，预计于2025年7月11日发布。玩家将扮演一只大而可爱的狗，在一个手工制作的冬季森林中探索，并与一个小孩一起装饰雪人。游戏特色包括：单人游玩、无失败状态、以及基于玩家选择和风格的互动体验。游戏世界由真实纸工艺模型构建，提供独特的视觉风格。玩家可以自由漫游露营区、森林小径、小溪和冰冻池塘等迷你开放世界，并与小孩互动以完成任务。游戏整体氛围轻松、治愈，适合全年龄段玩家。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Blender Studio的Dogwalk项目是否为真正的开源项目

不同观点：
• esperent认为Dogwalk项目不是开源项目，因为查看源代码需要每月支付11.50美元。他指出，只有在Steam页面上提到开源，这可能是一个错误，并建议联系Godot或Blender Studio以获得澄清。
• ssutch3支持esperent的观点，指出尽管声称是开源项目，但源代码被放置在付费墙之后，并提供了一个链接以示证明。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于“开源”的定义，特别是在付费墙后提供源代码是否仍符合开源的标准。
• 用户esperent和ssutch3都对项目声称开源但实际需要付费表示怀疑，并希望得到官方澄清。
• 提到的项目涉及Godot和Blender Studio，表明这些项目在开源社区中可能具有一定的影响力，因此用户对开源声明的准确性尤为关注。

data.title: Programming Language Theory has a public relations problem
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
编程语言理论（PLT）是一门兼具纯理论和实际应用的美丽学科，但外界常认为它晦涩难懂、不实用。这种误解源于几个问题：

1. **理论与应用的脱节**：PLT常被误认为具有实际应用，但许多理论工作仅在纯数学层面有价值，导致学习者困惑。
2. **缺乏积累性**：与其他数学领域不同，PLT的每个研究往往从基础开始，缺乏统一的定义和重用的定理，增加了学习难度。
3. **抽象化过度**：为了重用证明技术，PLT使用高度抽象的结构，导致初学者难以理解。
4. **难度高**：PLT涉及编程语言的复杂特性，变化细微且难以组合，使得研究和学习都非常困难。

解决方案包括：坦诚PLT的美丽在于其理论本身而非直接应用，为软件工程师提供入门材料，并尽量简化定理和证明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言理论（PLT）的实际应用及其对从业者的价值

不同观点：
• [pjc50] 认为，虽然计算机科学理论中有些内容具有实际应用价值，但很多理论的应用范围有限。即便有些理论可以应用，也需要很长时间才能转化为实际的实现，并且在推广过程中面临用户不愿改变的阻力。他以C++到Rust的过渡为例，说明这种转变的困难。他还赞赏C#逐渐引入功能性元素的做法。

• [throwaway81523] 主张PLT本质上是一个理论学科，从业者如果不热衷于理论，也不必设计前沿的语言或编译器。他们可以依靠研究机构产出的理论邻近内容保持前沿，例如Haskell。他还推荐了一些入门书籍，如Harper的《PFPL》，并认为Barendregt的文章可能过于数学化，不直接属于PL领域。

• [randomNumber7] 认为PLT可能有实际应用，但当前大多数常用语言的类型系统不够复杂。他认为λ演算过度关注数学和证明，对实际应用帮助不大。

• [fooker] 指出，虽然编程语言理论已被功能编程主导，但实践中使用的编程语言大多不是功能语言。这导致像他这样的编译器开发者很少能利用这些理论成果，使得工具在实践中有些笨拙。

• [johnecheck] 认为，新的思想需要新的表达方式，构建新语言是为了改善用户体验，虽然需要巨大的前期投入，但这是值得的。或者，也可以为了探索计算和形式语言的内在美而构建语言，不过他个人对此动机不太认同。

补充讨论：
• [rramadass] 强调PLT是一个跨学科领域，需要研究各种逻辑/数学/语言领域。他认为研究界未能为普通感兴趣的程序员提供一本概述/自顶向下的书籍，将所需知识整合成一个连贯的整体。他推荐了一些他认为有用的学习资源，如Slonneger和Kurtz的书以及Monin的理解形式方法。

争议焦点：
• PLT的实际应用价值以及其对从业者的意义。一部分人认为理论和实践之间存在脱节，另一部分人则认为理论对实际编程语言的发展有深远影响。

• λ演算在实际应用中的作用。有人认为它过于数学化，对实际编程帮助有限，而另一些人则认为它对理解和设计新语言至关重要。

• 对PLT学习资源的评价。一些评论者认为现有资源对初学者不够友好，需要更系统和易懂的入门书籍。

44553479.article_content:
Programming Language Theory has a public relations problem
13 Jul, 2025
Programming Language Theory (PLT) is one of my favourite areas of computer science yet I feel it's one of the most misunderstood by outsiders.
It's full of beautiful constructions and great ideas at the intersection of pure theory and practical applications. And yet outside of the PLT community, it's considered cryptic, hard, useless, not practical. The problems are similar to the public perception of pure maths ("why would I learn it?", "does it have any practical applications?") but somehow even worse.
How did it happen?
Problem 1: Theory vs applications
PLT can be done and appreciated as a pure maths subject, just like a beautiful construction proving an intricate topological theorem, or a stunning painting. It's an art. To fully appreciate it, you need some education.
A purely theoretical work is sometimes presented as having "practical applications". Sometimes the authors mean "it can be used to prove other theorems and the other 8 people interested in this topic might find it practically useful for that purpose". At other times, it's an overstated hope for potential future applications.
Imagine an experienced software engineer who got interested in PLT and wants to learn more. Someone told them that they should start with reading "The Lambda Calculus. Its Syntax and Semantics" by Barendregt. They go and struggle through unfamiliar notation, fighting to extract a drop of insight relevant to their experience. Finally, they understood the Church-Rosser theorem.
"What's Church-Rosser theorem good for?", software engineer asks. Oh, you see, it has
practical applications
, you just don't know enough to see it yet.
The engineer disappeared. His time was better spent learning a new Javascript framework - at least there he could see practical benefits.
Problem 2: Standing on the toes of the giants
Even simple-sounding theorems require heavy machinery. And that machinery is still being built, even though we started in the 30s.
How is that different from any other branch of mathematics? Well, if you take a look at undergraduate or graduate mathematics curriculum, you'll see that most subjects connect to one another. The build up on one another. Or there are celebrated "bridge" theorems, providing a way to translate results from one branch of mathematics to another.
Not so much in PLT. Each development, each proof starts close to starting from scratch. You won't find many authors reusing someone else's lemmas and theorems. Even definitions aren't agreed upon. So each paper can feel like starting from scratch.
Don't get me wrong, PLT researchers read each other's papers and do influence each other's work. But this influence happens at the level of techniques and approaches rather than formal reuse. Instead of building theorem-upon-theorem like in other mathematical fields, PLT researchers tend to adapt and modify each other's proof methods for their own ground-up constructions.
Problem 3: Abstraction creep
I mentioned that each paper, each problem might require a separate setup, with its own definitions, lemmas and theorems. Wouldn't it be nice if we could package common proof techniques as ready-made theorems and reuse them across many proofs?
It definitely would be nice but the price to pay is a very high level of abstraction. Think of it as a codebase which uses complicated architectural patterns, lots of indirection, many layers. Not in the spaghetti code kind of way, it's all necessary and used well - but there's a steep learning curve.
Just like with that codebase, where implementing each single piece of functionality from scratch would be
so much easier
without using so many abstractions, it's also the case for proofs using abstract methods. They are powerful but you lose intuitive clarity and make it harder for new people to jump in.
Problem 4: It's just hard
PLT is very hard. Minor changes to a language might break properties you rely on, language features don't compose nicely. The design space is vast, exploring each corner is expensive (how many production-grade compilers are there in the world?) and we've only had so much time.
On the other hand, PLT is about very concrete objects: programming languages. I can experiment with them, I can write interpreters, create my own toy language. Many people do! Why not learn some theory as well? How hard can it be?
It's an unpleasant surprise.
Solutions?
I can't dictate what people should and shouldn't do. But I'm well within my right to write down a wish-list:
Be honest and tell people that big part of motivation for PLT work is its inherent beauty and immediate applicability in software engineering scenarios is not the goal.
Create introductory materials for software engineers interested in PLT. It doesn't need to be comprehensive but it should provide motivation for why the theory exists, why it can be useful and why it is hard.
Keep your theorems and proofs as simple as possible. I know t

data.title: Daily Notes Considered Harmful
data.author: FigurativeVoid
data.article_summary: 文章主要批评了每日笔记（daily notes）的价值，认为它们通常不会被 revisit 或分享，只是制造了数字垃圾。笔记的价值应与其被访问和分享的频率成正比。文章建议专注于创建更可能被 revisit 或分享的笔记，比如一个持续更新的重点笔记（focus.md），用于追踪重要任务和次要任务。此外，针对重复出现的问题创建单独的笔记，并在需要时分享，能够增加笔记的价值。总的来说，作者强调笔记应减少无谓的记录，专注于实际有用的内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：笔记的价值和使用方法，包括是否应该频繁访问、是否应该分享、以及笔记的组织方式。

不同观点：
• **笔记的价值不应只看访问次数**：[ashton314] 认为笔记的价值在于帮助思考、解决问题和回忆，而不是访问频率。单纯依赖访问次数作为衡量标准是有害的，类似于数据囤积。
• **创建易于 revisit 和分享的笔记**：[emadda] 强调笔记的界面和内容的快速 recall 能力同样重要，并建议将答案放在笔记标题中以便于扫描。他认为分享笔记可以增加其价值，因为他自己有一个高效的笔记搜索工具。
• **个人化的笔记体验**：[sgoody] 表示笔记方式因人而异，日常笔记对他来说非常有效，解决了思考和记录的焦虑。而[massysett] 则持相反意见，认为笔记是个人使用的，分享会降低其价值，因为需要考虑他人理解和内容适当性。
• **每日笔记 vs. 每周笔记**：[jvanderbot] 和 [recursivegirth] 分别支持每日笔记和每周笔记。前者认为每日笔记提供了全新的开始，而后者认为每日笔记过于繁琐且不利于信息检索。
• **自动化和系统化的笔记方法**：[1123581321] 提倡自动附加参考的每日笔记系统，以减少时间和精力投入。而[sevensor] 则使用单一系统，无论是纸质还是数字笔记，都按日期和主题组织。
• **笔记的结构和创造性过程**：[thomascountz] 关注笔记结构如何影响创作过程，认为假设有观众可以引入有利的约束，但也可能阻碍重要见解。
• **技术进步对笔记的影响**：[thrwaway55] 质疑将笔记输入大语言模型的价值，认为原作者观点过时。
• **特定用途的笔记组织**：[stephenlf] 支持为特定问题和解决方案创建单独的笔记，认为这种方法在小团队中效果良好，但无法扩展。

补充讨论：
• **笔记的简要性**：[spicybbq] 指出其每日笔记非常简短，仅用于记录工作进展，以便于与经理会面和年度审查。
• **主题组织和日期模糊处理**：[spankibalt] 支持按主题组织笔记，同时模糊处理日期，认为这样更灵活且适用于不同用途。

争议焦点：
• **笔记的价值是否与访问次数相关**：[ashton314] 和 [emadda] 在这个问题上存在分歧，前者认为访问次数不重要，后者则强调 recall 能力的重要性。
• **笔记是否应分享**：[emadda] 认为分享笔记可以增加其价值，而 [massysett] 则坚持笔记的个人性，认为分享会降低其价值。
• **每日笔记的有效性**：[jvanderbot] 和 [recursivegirth] 对每日笔记和每周笔记的优劣有不同看法，前者认为每日笔记有助于管理复杂事务，后者则认为每周笔记更有效率。

44553873.article_content:
Daily notes considered harmful
2025-07-13
Daily notes are useless. The value of a note is directly proportional to the number of times it is visited. That value is exponentiated each time a note is shared. Daily notes aren't revisited and they aren't shared.
Daily notes look like this:
notes/
yyyy-mm-dd.md
yyyy-mm-dd.md
yyyy-mm-dd.md
On the surface, the idea of a note per day seems great. You plan out your day and track your work. You can revisit the past if needed. But you won't. All you are doing is generating digital clutter. You will also never share these notes, so the chance of their value increasing exponentially is zero.
Instead you should focus on creating notes that you are likely to revisit or likely to share.
Focus.md
I have one note that I visit all the time when I am working. It's a single Markdown file that I constantly update. It's essentially a to-do list that just helps me juggle all the things that I need to track. I call it focus.md
# Focus
Tasks that I have to do
## Periphery
Tasks that I have to be aware of, but I don't have to do.
It's nice because it lets me offload information that I don't need at hand and helps me focus on what I need to do.
Don't ask the same question twice
I try to never ask the same question twice. That means that when I do have a question, that question and its answer get a note.
They look something like this:
# Issue
## Issue details
## Resolution
Since I'm a programmer, I make a lot of these notes. I don't visit them very often, but I do revisit them if the same issue pops up again. But these notes find their value in being shared. If another person encounters the same issue, and I am able to help them fix it, then the note is worth the cost of its creation. I even add a lot of these notes to our documentation so I don't have to share them by hand.
It took me a while to figure out what's worth recording, and what isn't. And I am sure that it will be something different for you. But tools are supposed to prevent toil. Don't waste your time with daily notes.

44553873.article_summary: 文章主要批评了每日笔记（daily notes）的价值，认为它们通常不会被 revisit 或分享，只是制造了数字垃圾。笔记的价值应与其被访问和分享的频率成正比。文章建议专注于创建更可能被 revisit 或分享的笔记，比如一个持续更新的重点笔记（focus.md），用于追踪重要任务和次要任务。此外，针对重复出现的问题创建单独的笔记，并在需要时分享，能够增加笔记的价值。总的来说，作者强调笔记应减少无谓的记录，专注于实际有用的内容。
44553873.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：笔记的价值和使用方法，包括是否应该频繁访问、是否应该分享、以及笔记的组织方式。

不同观点：
• **笔记的价值不应只看访问次数**：[ashton314] 认为笔记的价值在于帮助思考、解决问题和回忆，而不是访问频率。单纯依赖访问次数作为衡量标准是有害的，类似于数据囤积。
• **创建易于 revisit 和分享的笔记**：[emadda] 强调笔记的界面和内容的快速 recall 能力同样重要，并建议将答案放在笔记标题中以便于扫描。他认为分享笔记可以增加其价值，因为他自己有一个高效的笔记搜索工具。
• **个人化的笔记体验**：[sgoody] 表示笔记方式因人而异，日常笔记对他来说非常有效，解决了思考和记录的焦虑。而[massysett] 则持相反意见，认为笔记是个人使用的，分享会降低其价值，因为需要考虑他人理解和内容适当性。
• **每日笔记 vs. 每周笔记**：[jvanderbot] 和 [recursivegirth] 分别支持每日笔记和每周笔记。前者认为每日笔记提供了全新的开始，而后者认为每日笔记过于繁琐且不利于信息检索。
• **自动化和系统化的笔记方法**：[1123581321] 提倡自动附加参考的每日笔记系统，以减少时间和精力投入。而[sevensor] 则使用单一系统，无论是纸质还是数字笔记，都按日期和主题组织。
• **笔记的结构和创造性过程**：[thomascountz] 关注笔记结构如何影响创作过程，认为假设有观众可以引入有利的约束，但也可能阻碍重要见解。
• **技术进步对笔记的影响**：[thrwaway55] 质疑将笔记输入大语言模型的价值，认为原作者观点过时。
• **特定用途的笔记组织**：[stephenlf] 支持为特定问题和解决方案创建单独的笔记，认为这种方法在小团队中效果良好，但无法扩展。

补充讨论：
• **笔记的简要性**：[spicybbq] 指出其每日笔记非常简短，仅用于记录工作进展，以便于与经理会面和年度审查。
• **主题组织和日期模糊处理**：[spankibalt] 支持按主题组织笔记，同时模糊处理日期，认为这样更灵活且适用于不同用途。

争议焦点：
• **笔记的价值是否与访问次数相关**：[ashton314] 和 [emadda] 在这个问题上存在分歧，前者认为访问次数不重要，后者则强调 recall 能力的重要性。
• **笔记是否应分享**：[emadda] 认为分享笔记可以增加其价值，而 [massysett] 则坚持笔记的个人性，认为分享会降低其价值。
• **每日笔记的有效性**：[jvanderbot] 和 [recursivegirth] 对每日笔记和每周笔记的优劣有不同看法，前者认为每日笔记有助于管理复杂事务，后者则认为每周笔记更有效率。

data.title: Adam Curtis's Shifty: When Britain was 'wild and extraordinary'
data.author: dijksterhuis
data.article_summary: Adam Curtis的新五集BBC纪录片《Shifty》探索了20世纪末的英国，通过一系列奇异的档案片段展现了当时社会的怪异与不确定性。影片融合了重大历史事件，如苏联解体和阿富汗战争，以及诸如前卫发型比赛、郊区线舞派对等超现实场景。Curtis利用这些片段讨论了社会变迁，尤其是过去的影像如何囚禁人们的思维。他重新使用了对前财政顾问Alan Budd的采访，揭示了撒切尔时代经济政策的真实意图。影片中，严肃的政治话题与喜剧元素并存，例如一只正在变性的狗，以及撒切尔手袋中残留的香水味，这些都象征着一个正在消逝的过去。Curtis认为撒切尔是一个悲剧性人物，她释放了无法控制的力量，试图创造一个政治影响力减弱的自由社会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Curtis纪录片的评价，特别是其内容的说服力和深度。

不同观点：
• 观点一：Curtis的纪录片表面上有说服力，但缺乏深度。[sandspar]认为Curtis的纪录片在观看时似乎很有道理，但经不起深入推敲。他将观看体验比作魔术表演，表面很吸引人，但背后可能缺乏实质内容。这暗示了Curtis的论证可能更多依赖于表现手法而非严谨的逻辑。

• 观点二：Curtis的纪录片对年轻观众有吸引力。[sandspar]提到，Curtis的纪录片在年轻观众（例如20岁左右）中可能更受欢迎，暗示其内容或风格可能更符合年轻人的口味，或者更容易被表面的炫目效果所吸引。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Curtis的纪录片是否只是表面精彩而缺乏深度。这涉及到纪录片的核心价值——是注重表现形式还是内容深度。一些人可能认为他的作品在视觉和叙述上非常吸引人，而另一些人则质疑其论证的严谨性和深度。

• 自我反思：[sandspar]在评论开头用了一句半开玩笑的话（“Maybe that's a bit harsh.”），显示出对自己观点的某种反思或不确定性，似乎也在平衡自己对Curtis作品的批评态度。这表明评论者意识到自己的观点可能带有主观偏见或苛刻。

总结来看，讨论围绕Curtis纪录片的形式与内容深度展开，重点在于其作品是否能够在吸引眼球的同时经得起深入分析。

44554565.article_content:
Image caption,
Avant-garde hairstyles are one of the many strange elements of British life highlighted in Shifty
Samuel Spencer
BBC
Published
13 June 2025
The documentary filmmaker Adam Curtis gives a guide to some of the key moments from his new series Shifty.
In his documentaries, Adam Curtis has taken us everywhere from Russia during the breakdown of the Soviet Union, in
TraumaZone
, to the war in Afghanistan, in
Bitter Lake
.
Now Curtis, whose work has been called
"dazzling" and "terrifying"
by critics, has set his sights on Britain at the end of the 20th century for the five-part BBC series
Shifty
.
This time Curtis's signature style sees him use a bizarre array of archive clips to explore, he says, how "life in Britain today has become strange - a hazy dream-like flux in which no-one can predict what is coming next".
In Shifty, clips of the major players of the era â Prime Ministers Margaret Thatcher, John Major and Tony Blair â exist alongside surreal moments sourced from the BBC's extensive archives, like avant-garde hairdressing competitions, suburban line dancing parties and children hot-wiring a tractor.
To the uninitiated, his documentaries can feel impenetrable, so we spoke to Curtis to curate and explain some of the key clips from the new series.
Curtis also suggested a title for each clip that perfectly places viewers into the strange and murky world of Shifty.
'One of the few moments of honesty'
Media caption,
'The government adviser suspecting treachery'
One section details the rise of the musical remixes in the 1980s, and its societal implications â how, in Curtis's words, "we are trapped by a cascade of endlessly replayed images, songs, dreams from the past".
However, he admits, "that's the way this series was made, so I'm just as bad. If it's become a prison, I may be one of the jailers."
One way Curtis remixes the past is by reusing an interview with Sir Alan Budd that Curtis filmed for the 1992 documentary
Pandora's Box
.
In a remarkably honest interview, the one-time chief economic adviser to the Treasury during Thatcher's tenure worries that "the people making the policy decisionsâ¦ never believed for a moment this was the correct way to bring down inflation.
"They did, however, see that it would be a very, very good way to raise unemployment, and raising unemployment was an extremely desirable way of reducing the strength of the working class."
"I've always been fascinated by that interview that Budd gave," says Curtis. "It's one of the few moments of honesty I've ever had from someone in power like that being interviewed."
'A past that was about to go'
Media caption,
'Bruno - the dog that is shifting sex'
As a young BBC employee, Curtis worked on That's Life. The show combined consumer affairs with lighter stories â most famously,
a dog that could 'say' the word sausages.
Curtis credits his ability to juggle tragic and comic tones to this early role: "It showed me that you could go from a badly-built housing estate built on poisonous waste ground to a talking dog."
In Shifty, clips of societal unrest exist alongside Bruno, a dog who is, according to his vet, "changing his sex" â their male organs disappearing and their female ones developing.
Curtis says that it was Bruno's owner that drew him to the clip: "The way she's sitting and her hair," he says, "it felt like a past that was about to go."
Animals in his work can often represent our secret lives, he says â "they are these creatures who live with us who probably have a lot of hidden knowledge about us."
For Curtis, animals also counterpoint what he calls the "highly pretentious" elements of his work: "They just entertain people."
'A tragic figure'
Media caption,
'Margaret Thatcher's handbag and the ghostly perfume'
In this clip, an archivist at Cambridge University takes one of Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's handbags out of a box, noting how the bag still smells strongly of her perfume.
Similarly, Thatcher's presence can be felt in much of the series, as we see the effects of
her policies in the 1980s and 90s
.
Before Thatcher became Prime Minister in 1979, Curtis argues there was "a collective model of society, where people came together in factories, were exploited, then realised they had power as a collective group."
He feels, however, that the closure of industries like mining led to "a society full of fragmented individuals who were powerful in the way they thought about their own desires, but actually on their own were powerless."
Despite this, Curtis sees Thatcher as a "tragic figure", who unleashed forces she could not control.
"She was the last politician who had an idea of how to change the country," he explains. "She wanted to create a society in which politics doesn't have as much effect as it did, and should allow individuals to be loose and free."
'Ever more irrational assumptions'
Media caption,
'In one universe, Stephen Hawking says goodnight to his child'
Another recurring character in Shifty

data.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Django
data.author: davepeck
data.article_summary: Django于2025年7月13日迎来20周年生日！自2005年Jacob Kaplan-Moss首次提交代码以来，Django已发布400多个版本。为庆祝这一时刻，官方推出了一个特别网站，展示全球线上线下庆祝活动，包括问答、社区成就展示等。同时，Django软件基金会呼吁大家捐款支持项目，目标是在20天内获得200名新捐助者，每人捐赠至少20美元，其中至少20人成为每月定期捐助者。截至2025年7月13日，已完成目标的25.6%，募集到76,707美元。展望未来，Django计划继续发布新版本，扩展生态系统，并保持包容和支持的开发者社区。

44552500.article_content:
Happy 20th birthday Django!
Posted by
Thibaud Colas & Benjamin Balder Bach
on July 13, 2025
On July 13th 2005, Jacob Kaplan-Moss made the first commit to the public repository that would become Django. Twenty years and 400+ releases later, here we are –
Happy 20th birthday Django! 🎉
Join the celebrations
We want to share this special occasion with you all! Our new
20-years of Django website
showcases all online and local events happening around the world, through all of 2025. As well as other opportunities to celebrate!
Expect birthday cake 🎂 and singing Happy Birthday
A special quiz or two? see who knows all about Django trivia
Showcase of great community achievements
View our 20th birthday website
Support Django
As a birthday gift of sorts, consider whether you or your employer can support the project via donations to our non-profit Django Software Foundation. For this special event, we want to set a special goal!
Over the next 20 days, we want to see 200 new donors, supporting Django with $20 or more, with at least 20 monthly donors.
Help us making this happen:
Donate on the Django website
Donate on GitHub sponsors
Or check out how to
become a Corporate Member
Once you’ve done it, post with #DjangoBirthday and tag us
on Mastodon
/
on Bluesky
/
on X
/
on LinkedIn
so we can say thank you!
26%
Of our US $300,000.00 goal for 2025, as of July 13th, 2025, we are at:
25.6% funded
$76,707 donated
Donate to support Django
The next 20 years
20 years is a long time in open source – and we want to keep Django thriving for many more, so it keeps on being the web framework for perfectionists with deadlines as the industry evolves. We don’t know how the web will change it that time, but from Django, you can expect:
Many new releases, each with years of support
Thousands more packages in our
thriving ecosystem
An inclusive and supportive community with hundreds of thousands of developers
Happy 20th birthday, Django!

data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 科学家发现一颗巨大气态行星HIP 67522 b，围绕年轻恒星HIP 67522运行时，引发恒星表面产生巨大耀斑，这种现象前所未见。该行星距离恒星极近，轨道距离仅为水星与太阳距离的五分之一，公转周期仅7天。其与恒星磁场的相互作用可能是引发耀斑的原因，耀斑可能逐渐剥离行星的大气层。HIP 67522 b体积接近木星，但质量仅5%，大气主要由氢和氦组成，未来可能演变为亚海王星。研究利用了NASA的TESS和欧空局的CHEOPS卫星数据，揭示了这颗行星的特殊环境和演化前景。

44554498.article_content:
Will Dunham
July 7, 2025 at 10:56 AM
0
Copied
By Will Dunham
WASHINGTON (Reuters) -Scientists are tracking a large gas planet experiencing quite a quandary as it orbits extremely close to a young star - a predicament never previously observed.
This exoplanet, as planets beyond our solar system are called, orbits its star so tightly that it appears to trigger flares from the stellar surface - larger than any observed from the sun - reaching several million miles (km) into space that over time may strip much of this unlucky world's atmosphere.
The phenomenon appears to be caused by the planet's interaction with the star's magnetic field, according to the researchers. And this star is a kind known to flare, especially when young.
"A young star of this type is an angry beast, especially if you're sitting as close up as this planet does," said Netherlands Institute for Radio Astronomy astrophysicist Ekaterina Ilin, lead author of the study published in the journal Nature.
The star, called HIP 67522, is slightly more massive than the sun and is located about 407 light-years from Earth in the constellation Centaurus. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km).
This star and planet, as well as a second smaller gas planet also detected in this planetary system, are practically newborns. Whereas the sun and our solar system's planets are roughly 4.5 billion years old, this star is about 17 million years old, with its planets slightly younger.
The planet, named HIP 67522 b, has a diameter almost the size of Jupiter, our solar system's largest planet, but with only 5% of Jupiter's mass. That makes it one of the puffiest exoplanets known, with a consistency reminiscent of cotton candy (candy floss).
It orbits five times closer to its star than our solar system's innermost planet Mercury orbits the sun, needing only seven days to complete an orbit.
A flare is an intense eruption of electromagnetic radiation emanating from the outermost part of a star's atmosphere, called the corona. So how does HIP 67522 b elicit huge flares from the star? As it orbits, it apparently interacts with the star's magnetic field - either through its own magnetic field or perhaps through the presence of conducting material such as iron in the planet's composition.
"We don't know for sure what the mechanism is. We think it is plausible that the planet moves within the star's magnetic field and whips up a wave that travels along magnetic field lines to the star. When the wave reaches the stellar corona, it triggers flares in large magnetic field loops that store energy, which is released by the wave," Ilin said.
"As it moves through the field like a boat on a lake, it creates waves in its wake," Ilin added. "The flares these waves trigger when they crash into the star are a new phenomenon. This is important because it had never been observed before, especially at the intensity detected."
The researchers believe it is a specific type of wave called an Alfvén wave, named for 20th century Swedish physicist and Nobel Prize laureate Hannes Alfvén, that propagates due to the interaction of magnetic fields.
The flares may heat up and inflate the planet's atmosphere, which is dominated by hydrogen and helium. Being lashed by these flares could blast away lighter elements from the atmosphere and reduce the planet's mass over perhaps hundreds of millions of years.
"At that time, it will have lost most if not all the light elements, and become what's called a sub-Neptune - a gas planet smaller than Neptune," Ilin said, referring to the smallest of our solar system's gas planets.
The researchers used observations by two space telescopes: NASA's TESS, short for Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, and the European Space Agency's CHEOPS, short for CHaracterising ExOPlanet Satellite.
The plight of HIP 67522 b illustrates the many circumstances under which exoplanets exist.
"It is certainly no sheltered youth for this planet. But I am not sad about it. I enjoy diversity in all things nature, and what this planet will eventually become - perhaps a sub-Neptune rich in heavy elements that did not evaporate - is no less fascinating than what we observe today."
(Reporting by Will Dunham, Editing by Rosalba O'Brien)

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Peter Falk在节目中表现的评价

不同观点：
• 观点一：B1FF_PSUVM认为Peter Falk的表现非常出色。他将Falk的表演描述为一种“出色的技巧”（brilliant hack），并强调Falk通过扮演一个朴实、笨拙的角色赢得了观众的笑声。B1FF_PSUVM特别指出，Falk并没有采用传统的“激烈批评或嘲讽”（roasting）方式，而是通过一种更为谦卑、顺从的表演风格（forelock tugging）赢得了观众的青睐。

• 观点二：未直接表达但可推断出的潜在观点是，可能有人认为Falk的表演缺乏挑战性或创新性，因为B1FF_PSUVM提到了“没有采用激烈的嘲讽方式”（No roasting involved），暗示另一种表演风格可能也会被期待或争议。

补充讨论：
• Falk的角色被具体描述为“aw shucks”类型，这是一种典型的谦逊、朴实的角色形象，通常用来形容那些故意表现得笨拙、朴素以赢得观众喜爱的角色。
• 评论中提到的“just forelock tugging all the way”是一种比喻，指的是一种非常恭敬、顺从的态度，这可能是在暗示Falk通过这种谦逊的态度获得了观众的好感。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对“brilliant hack”的评价，一些人可能认为这种表演方式过于简单或缺乏深度，而另一些人（如B1FF_PSUVM）则可能认为这种朴实无华的表演正是Falk的魅力所在。

data.title: How to put your phone down and get back into habit of reading books (2024)
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了如何减少手机使用，重拾阅读习惯。主要建议包括：

1. 将手机放远，最好不在同一房间，以减少干扰。
2. 阅读纸质书，并做笔记，限制社交媒体使用。
3. 重新训练大脑，从少量阅读开始，逐渐增加时间。
4. 找到最佳的阅读时间和地点，比如早晨。
5. 不要把阅读当作任务，从有趣的书开始。
6. 利用读书俱乐部和图书馆获取动力和灵感。
7. 音频书和优质电视剧也是不错的选择，可以帮助重拾阅读习惯。

文章强调，通过减少手机依赖和选择适合自己的阅读方式，可以有效提升专注力和阅读体验。

After an English academic at Oxford complained about students’ attention spans, we get experts’ tips on enjoying the written word
Sarah Phillips
Fri 11 Oct 2024 09.02 EDT

ir Jonathan Bate, a professor of English literature at Oxford, this week voiced his concern at the “attrition of attention span”, as witnessed through his undergraduates’ inability to keep up with reading lists. “Now, instead of three novels in a week, many students will struggle to get through one novel in three weeks,” he told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme.
It isn’t just young people who are finding it hard to concentrate on books. In July, the UK charity
The Reading Agency
found that only
half of UK adults now read regularly for pleasure
. So how can we put our phones down and get back into reading?
1. Keep your phone as far away as possible
“If you’re going to sit down with a book, leave your phone somewhere else,” says Tanya Goodin, a digital detox campaigner and the author of
My Brain Has Too Many Tabs Open
. “
This means it is not visible and not in the same room, because self-control doesn’t work.” Goodin points to
research
into what happens to our problem-solving ability and IQ when we have our phones in close proximity: “It has been shown that only when our device is in a different room do we really have the full ability to focus.”
Cal Newport, a productivity expert, agrees that out of sight is out of mind. “Keep your phone plugged in at a set location when you’re at home,” he advises. “If you need to look things up or check your messages, go to where the phone is.” If your phone is not by your side, then “if you’re reading and feel a tinge of boredom it’s much easier to push through”.
2. Read
physical books – and make notes
Damian Barr, the author and host of
The Big Scottish Book Club
, tries to carry a book at all times: “If I haven’t got something with me, I can’t read it. Books always lose against social media in the competition on my phone, so I need actual paper.” He limits his social media usage with blocker apps, “which I can override but at least it makes me more aware of how much time I am spending on them”.
Lara Feigel, an author and professor of English at King’s College London, says her students are struggling to keep up with the reading. “I urge them to buy actual copies of books rather than reading online,” she says, “and to makes notes by hand on the books – sometimes I ask them to bring their books in and show me the underlinings and scribbles”.
“Books are part of the pleasure of reading,” says Goodin. “I love getting a new book, smelling it and cracking open the spine.” This can “give you a dopamine hit more than a screen”.
3. Retrain your brain
“Reading is a marathon, not a sprint,” says Daisy Buchanan, the host of
You’re Booked podcast
and author of the forthcoming
Read Yourself Happy
. “Like exercise, reading came naturally to us as children, but we have acquired a lot of noise and distraction. Start with the smallest amount of time you can and build it back up again.”
Goodin suggests setting a target of 10 pages at a time.
4. Work out your optimum time and place to read
For Buchanan, this is first thing in the morning. “When I wake up my brain is on fire with thoughts and anxiety. If I make the effort to pick up a book first, and not my phone, reading gives my mind the information it is craving, slowing it down and providing it with something to focus on.”
5. Don’t treat reading
as if it’s a chore
Important books are the goal not the starting point, says Buchanan. “You need to begin with books for pleasure and joy in order to work up to things that really challenge you.” When Buchanan’s brain got “hijacked” by a smartphone, she returned to the books she had enjoyed as a child, such as Judy Blume, to rekindle her love of literature. “We’re not going to read if it is virtuous and worthy.”
Joining a book club can give you the motivation to keep going to the end of a book, says Goodin.
She also recommends rediscovering libraries as a place to
find inspiration
.
6.
Don’t forget audiobooks (and
good TV)
“If you haven’t read for a while, an audiobook might be a good gateway drug to get back into the habit,” says Goodin, especially if you can multitask and listen while commuting or walking the dog. Turning off notifications when you listen is a must, she says.

data.title: Show HN: FFmpeg in plain English – LLM-assisted FFmpeg in the browser
data.author: bjano
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了使用FFmpeg工具处理视频和音频文件的基本步骤。用户可以在FFmpeg加载后添加输入文件，并通过示例操作如保留视频前20秒、提取音频为mp3文件、将mp3音频混入视频等进行编辑。最后，运行处理并完成操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于LLM（大语言模型）和FFmpeg的终端命令生成工具及其应用

不同观点：
• Hassanijaz和kkukshtel分享了他们使用LLM在终端中生成FFmpeg命令的工具和经验。Hassanijaz开发了langterm，而kkukshtel使用Claude Code，两者都强调了通过自然语言处理复杂命令的优势。
• jjcm对ffmpegwasm在浏览器中的实现表示了兴趣，并询问了具体的实现细节，表明在浏览器中运行FFmpeg的挑战。
• orderone_ai赞赏这种工具对普通用户的便利性，并指出这是"聊天驱动用户体验"趋势的一个例子，表明了这种趋势的广泛应用潜力。
• jjbinx007分享了使用Gemini修复损坏视频文件的经验，提出了Untrunc作为FFmpeg的替代方案，强调了LLM在问题诊断中的实用性。

补充讨论：
• raincole关注ffmpeg在浏览器中的工作原理，提出了是否通过WebAssembly实现的问题。
• baobabKoodaa认为这种LLM包装器是薄层应用的完美案例。
• toddmorey推荐了Warp终端，并分享了其在视频转换和文件处理中的应用经验。
• bsenftner指出工具在处理带有空格的长文件名时的不足，建议增加文件名处理功能。
• p0w3n3d引用了一句幽默的拒绝语句，但没有提供实质性意见。
• danielvaughn分享了他在实现类似工具时遇到的困难，特别是在LLM生成FFmpeg命令方面的挑战。
• somesun提到一个类似的网站ffmpeg.app，提供了另一个可视化FFmpeg工具的例子。
• pdyc介绍了自己开发的视频编辑工具，该工具通过可视化界面生成FFmpeg命令，解决了命令行调整困难的问题。

争议焦点：
• 工具在处理复杂文件名（如带有空格的文件名）时的局限性。
• LLM生成FFmpeg命令的实际效果和实现难度存在不同看法，部分用户如kkukshtel和toddmorey认为效果很好，而danielvaughn则认为实现难度较大。

总结：讨论围绕基于LLM的终端命令生成工具展开，参与者分享了各自的工具、实现经验和使用建议，同时指出了工具在处理复杂文件名等方面的局限性和改进空间。

data.title: Stellantis declares bankruptcy in China, with $1B in debts
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 湖南长沙法院宣布广汽菲亚特克莱斯勒合资企业破产，标志着Stellantis在中国的业务正式结束。该合资企业成立于2011年，由塞尔吉奥·马尔乔内推动，旨在帮助菲亚特克莱斯勒与中国广汽集团共同征服全球最大汽车市场。初期投资170亿元，年产30万辆车，但2017年达到销量高峰后迅速下滑，主要由于未能适应中国市场对新能源和电动车的需求，仍专注于传统燃油车。2022年进入重组程序，五次拍卖均失败，最终负债超过81亿元，资产仅19亿元。法院裁定破产清算。这一失败反映了Stellantis及其他西方车企在面对中国电动车革命时的适应无力，加之与广汽关系恶化和地缘政治影响，最终导致退出中国市场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Stellantis集团在汽车市场中的表现及面临的挑战

不同观点：
• **供应链和市场问题**：[zihotki] 指出Stellantis面临供应链问题、新车发布延迟以及高昂的价格，特别是在荷兰，电动汽车充电设施不足，导致消费者对电动车持犹豫态度。电力成本高也是影响因素，因此混合动力车对很多人来说更实际。
• **Stellantis内部问题**：[Animats] 认为Stellantis的问题并非行业普遍问题，而是其内部管理问题，引用经销商致CEO的信说明公司内部困境，甚至提到克莱斯勒仅剩的一条小型货车生产线。
• **盈利能力与债务问题**：[aetherspawn] 作为汽车零部件供应商，质疑大型汽车公司如何在当前环境下保持盈利，指出高研发成本和新的高级驾驶辅助系统（ADAS）法规带来的财务压力，并暗示许多公司依赖债务运营。
• **品牌存续的疑问**：[rsynnott] 表示对Stellantis持续运营的惊讶，指出其旗下的许多品牌让人感觉早已不再生产，但也提到其中国子公司仍盈利。
• **战略失误**：[speedgoose] 批评Stellantis的短期利润最大化策略和制造平庸汽车的策略，认为这是公司困境的主因。
• **中国市场表现**：[cyp0633] 指出Stellantis在中国市场的销量早在电动车流行前就已下滑，并讽刺其通过Leapmotor在中国市场的存在。
• **政治与经济反思**：[WhereIsTheTruth] 将Stellantis的问题归因于西方精英为短期利益背叛民众，导致现在回归本土市场困难。
• **历史与文化因素**：[SV_BubbleTime] 回顾历史，认为Stellantis在管理和决策上每一步都走错，甚至开玩笑地猜测公司可能在“加速自我毁灭”。
• **合并与品牌选择**：[tibbydudeza] 认为Silverado车型可能拯救公司，问题主要在Fiat一侧，并建议Peugeot与Renault合并会更好。
• **技术转型迟缓**：[aussieguy1234] 认为Stellantis的困境源于未及时拥抱新技术，尤其是电动车技术。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Stellantis内部管理问题与市场策略之间的矛盾是主要争议点，一些人认为其内部问题更为严重，而另一些人则关注市场环境和外部因素的影响。
• **各地区市场差异**：评论中提到荷兰和中国的市场差异，指出不同地区消费者对电动车和混合动力车的接受程度不同。
• **对品牌未来发展的担忧**：多位评论者对Stellantis旗下品牌的存续表示怀疑，并对其长期发展策略提出质疑。

44555836.article_content:
Advertising
It's the official end of an ambitious project launched nearly fifteen years ago: the court in Changsha, Hunan province, has declared the Gac-Fiat Chrysler joint venture bankrupt, putting a definitive end to the industrial presence of
Stellantis
via this entity in China.
This joint venture, created in 2011 at the instigation of Sergio Marchionne,
was to enable Fiat Chrysler to conquer the world's largest automobile market alongside Chinese giant GAC Group.
At the time, the ambitions were immense: 17 billion yuan in investment (around 2.3 billion euros), two plants in Guangzhou and Changsha, a capacity of 300,000 vehicles a year, and a range adapted to local tastes, including Jeep Renegade, Compass, Cherokee and the Fiat Viaggio and Ottimo.
Advertising
But after a sales peak in 2017 (over 200,000 units), the descent into hell was swift. Unable to keep up with the Chinese market,
dominated by new technologies and electrified vehicles,
Gac-FCA remained focused on thermal models that were increasingly unattractive to Chinese consumers.
In 2022, the company entered restructuring proceedings. Since then, no attempt has been made to sell assets: five public auctions have remained empty, despite the sale of land, equipment and two factories. The result: liabilities of over 8.1 billion yuan (approx. $1.1 billion), including 4 billion in undisputed debts, against assets estimated at just 1.9 billion.
In the absence of an agreement with creditors, the court declared the company liquidated.
Advertising
This failure also symbolizes the inability of Stellantis, like other Western manufacturers,
to adapt to China's electric revolution, led by ultra-competitive local brands.
Converting sites from fossil-fired to electric power would have required colossal investments that no investor was willing to make.
The geopolitical context and deteriorating relations between Stellantis and GAC have not helped matters. After the FCA-PSA merger, Carlos Tavares had tried to regain control of the joint venture, but GAC had opposed him, denouncing what it considered unsuitable governance and a regulatory climate unfavorable to foreign groups.
Advertising
With this bankruptcy, Stellantis definitively turns the page on a part of the Asian strategy inherited from Marchionne. A page fraught with symbolism... and a billion-dollar liability to wipe out.

data.title: The Scourge of Arial (2001)
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: Arial是一种广泛使用的字体，常见于微软产品中，尽管其设计并不特别美观或独特。它实际上是Helvetica的替代品，后者是20世纪后期非常流行的字体。由于Adobe在PostScript语言中使用了Helvetica等字体，使得它们在桌面出版界广泛传播。然而，Adobe对Type 1字体技术的垄断引发竞争，苹果和微软合作开发TrueType格式以打破Adobe的垄断。与此同时，市场上出现了PostScript的替代品，其中包括Birmy的产品，它使用了与Helvetica相似的Arial字体。Arial在设计上模仿了Helvetica的比例和重量，但细节上有所不同，对于普通用户难以区分，但对设计师而言差别明显。Monotype在设计Arial时本可以完全复制Helvetica，但他们选择做了一些改动，使得Arial成为一种“看似相似但不同”的字体。

44555317.article_content:
Browse categories
Arial is everywhere. If you don’t know what it is, you don’t use a modern personal computer. Arial is a font that is familiar to anyone who uses Microsoft products, whether on a PC or a Mac. It has spread like a virus through the typographic landscape and illustrates the pervasiveness of Microsoft’s influence in the world.
Arial’s ubiquity is not due to its beauty. It’s actually rather homely. Not that homeliness is necessarily a bad thing for a typeface. With typefaces, character and history are just as important. Arial, however, has a rather dubious history and not much character. In fact, Arial is little more than a shameless impostor.
Throughout the latter half of the twentieth century, one of the most popular typefaces in the western world was Helvetica. It was developed by the Haas Foundry of Switzerland in the 1950s. Later, Haas merged with Linotype and Helvetica was heavily promoted. More weights were added and it really began to catch on.
An icon of the Swiss school of typography, Helvetica swept through the design world in the ’60s and became synonymous with modern, progressive, cosmopolitan attitudes. With its friendly, cheerful appearance and clean lines, it was universally embraced for a time by both the corporate and design worlds as a nearly perfect typeface to be used for anything and everything. “When in doubt, use Helvetica” was a common rule.
As it spread into the mainstream in the ’70s, many designers tired of it and moved on to other typographic fashions, but by then it had become a staple of everyday design and printing. So in the early ’80s when Adobe developed the PostScript page description language, it was no surprise that they chose Helvetica as one of the basic four fonts to be included with every PostScript interpreter they licensed (along with Times, Courier, and Symbol). Adobe licensed its fonts from the original foundries, demonstrating their respect and appreciation for the integrity of type, type foundries and designers. They perhaps realized that if they had used knock-offs of popular typefaces, the professional graphic arts industry—a key market—would not accept them.
By the late eighties, the desktop publishing phenomenon was in full swing. Led by the Macintosh and programs like PageMaker, and made possible by Adobe’s PostScript page description language, anyone could do near professional-quality typesetting on relatively inexpensive personal computers.
But there was a problem. There were two kinds of PostScript fonts: Type 1 and Type 3. Type 1 fonts included “hints” that improved the quality of output dramatically over Type 3 fonts. Adobe provided information on making Type 3 fonts, but kept the secrets of the superior Type 1 font technology to itself. If you wanted Type 1 fonts, Adobe was the only source. Anyone else who wanted to make or sell fonts had to settle for the inferior Type 3 format. Adobe wanted the high end of the market all to itself.
By 1989, a number of companies were hard at work trying to crack the Type 1 format or devise alternatives. Apple and Microsoft signed a cross-licensing agreement to create an alternative to Adobe’s technology. While Microsoft worked on TrueImage, a page description language, Apple developed the TrueType format. TrueType was a more open format and was compatible with—but not dependent on—PostScript. This effectively forced Adobe’s hand, causing them to release the secrets of the Type 1 format to save themselves from irrelevancy.
Around the same time, PostScript “clones” were being developed to compete with Adobe. These PostScript “work-alikes” were usually bundled with “look-alike” fonts, since the originals were owned by Adobe’s business partners. One PostScript clone, sold by Birmy, featured a Helvetica substitute developed by Monotype called Arial.
Arial appears to be a loose adaptation of Monotype’s venerable Grotesque series, redrawn to match the proportions and weight of Helvetica. At a glance, it looks like Helvetica, but up close it’s different in dozens of seemingly arbitrary ways. Because it matched Helvetica’s proportions, it was possible to automatically substitute Arial when Helvetica was specified in a document printed on a PostScript clone output device. To the untrained eye, the difference was hard to spot. (See “
How to Spot Arial
”) After all, most people would have trouble telling the difference between a serif and a sans serif typeface. But to an experienced designer, it was like asking for Jimmy Stewart and getting Rich Little.
What is really strange about Arial is that it appears that Monotype was uncomfortable about doing a direct copy of Helvetica. They could very easily have done that and gotten away with it. Many type manufacturers in the past have done knock-offs of Helvetica that were indistinguishable or nearly so. For better or worse, in many countries—particularly the U.S.—while typeface names can be protected legally, typeface designs themselves are difficult to protect. So, i

data.title: James Webb, Hubble space telescopes face reduction in operations
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: NASA's Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes (JWST) face operational cuts due to budget limitations. Hubble's budget has remained flat for a decade, losing 30% of its purchasing power to inflation. The Trump administration's proposed 2026 budget aims to cut JWST's funding by 25%, from $187 million to $140 million, and Hubble's from $93.3 million to $85 million. These cuts may result in reduced telescope modes and less user support. JWST, still in its prime mission, may see a 25-35% reduction in science operations, affecting its 17 observation modes due to staff cuts. The budget shortfalls could decrease observation efficiency and limit available support for astronomers.

44555804.article_content:
The James Webb Space Telescope is pictured here before being folded up for launch. Credit: NASA
Key Takeaways:
NASA's Hubble and James Webb telescopes face operational cuts due to budget limitations.
Reduced funding may lead to fewer available telescope modes and less user support.
Hubble's budget has remained flat for a decade, decreasing its purchasing power.
“It’s fewer people, really,” said Neill Reid.
Key takeaways sponsored by
The Space Store
See a mistake?
Contact us
.
The teams operating the Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) — NASA’s two most in-demand observatories and among its most scientifically productive missions — are preparing to reduce operations due to funding shortfalls, officials said last week at the summer meeting of the American Astronomical Society (AAS) in Anchorage, Alaska.
The comments came at a June 10 town hall held by the Space Telescope Science Institute (STScI), which is based in Baltimore, Maryland, and operates JWST and Hubble for NASA.
Speaking at the town hall, Neill Reid, multi-mission project scientist at STScI, said the institute is looking at a likely reduction of around 25 to 35 percent in science operations for JWST. The institute is also likely to reduce or drop support for several of Hubble’s instruments; they will still be available for observations, but the telescope’s staff will no longer be able to support them with regular calibration updates.
The threats to JWST and Hubble are due to a combination of factors, some of which have been brewing for years. Over the past year, NASA and STScI officials have warned of budgetary challenges and operational reductions due to flat budgets and inflation.
Another factor is funding cuts to both telescopes contained in the Trump administration’s budget proposal for 2026 — especially JWST, which would see its operating budget cut by 25 percent relative to planned 2024 operations, from $187 million to $140 million.
The cut to Hubble — down from $93.3 million in planned funds for 2024 to $85 million in 2026 — is less of a surprise. The Biden administration’s
2025 budget request
, which was never enacted, also contained a planned reduction in Hubble funding, down to $87.5 million in 2026. In 2024, NASA conducted
a review
of Hubble’s operations, seeking to reduce costs.
A
document
posted to NASA’s website May 30 says the Trump administration’s budget proposal “supports continued operations” of Hubble and JWST “at slightly reduced budget levels which assume operational efficiencies in FY 2026 and out.”
Budgetary issues
Speaking at the AAS town hall, STScI’s Neill Reid said Hubble’s budget has remained essentially flat over the past decade while inflation has increased, resulting in a drop in spending power of 30 percent. Any additional cuts to Hubble’s budget “will result in significant loss to science,” an STScI slide stated.
Part of the challenge facing Hubble, which launched in 1990, is that it “has lasted longer than people expected,” Reid told
Astronomy
. “NASA’s looking at how much money it has. And it’s trying to do as many things as possible. … If it were to build up the Hubble budget, it would be cutting something else.” STScI has made Hubble’s operation leaner, but eventually, the only way to save more money is to “stop doing things,” Reid said.
Unlike Hubble, JWST is still in the midst of its prime mission. The telescope, which cost $10 billion to construct, was launched in 2021 and began operations the following year. NASA originally hoped the telescope would operate for 10 years, but thanks to a highly accurate launch, there is enough fuel on board to last for more than 20 years.
Even if the Trump administration’s proposed budget cuts are rejected by Congress, JWST was already facing budgetary pressures. That’s partly because the observatory’s operations budget set by NASA in 2011 was idealistically low, said Reid.
“There was a sound amount of optimism that went into some of those, and there’s also been inflation,” said Reid. “So then you have the [presidential budget request] that comes in and cuts more. So we may be looking at reducing operations by 25 to 35 percent next year.”
Reid said STScI does not yet have a specific plan to deal with JWST’s budget shortfalls, but it will almost certainly involve reducing staff.
“It’s fewer people, really,” Neill Reid, multi-mission project scientist at STScI, told
Astronomy
. “[JWST has] got 17 different modes. Each of those modes needs people to support it, to calibrate it, to keep it going. So, if you cut the funding, you have fewer people. And you can’t ask people to do twice as much work. So what will happen is that there will be potentially fewer modes available. There will be less user support.”

44521108.article_content:
'Chimpfluencers' Are Sticking Grass in Their Ears And Butts in Latest Viral Trend
Nature
10 July 2025
By
Michael Irving
Chimps have been seen following a bizarre new trend.
(Jake Brooker/Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust)
If chimpanzees had access to TikTok, the platform might soon be flooded with videos of 'chimpfluencers' wearing grass in their ears and butts – the latest trend going around a chimp sanctuary in Africa.
In August 2023, at the Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust sanctuary in Zambia, a trendsetting chimp named Juma was seen sticking a piece of grass into his ear, deep enough to stay there on its own. Within a week the fad went viral, as four other chimps in the group started copying his unusual accessory.
Not to be outdone, later that month Juma debuted a risqué variation: he inserted a blade of grass into his rectum, and left it dangling. This unorthodox trend also caught on, with five other chimps adopting the strange new fashion.
Related:
Bored Capuchin Monkeys Are Kidnapping Howler Babies in Weird New 'Trend'
The behavior fascinated researchers observing the captive chimpanzees (
Pan troglodytes
) . The grass didn't seem to serve a biological purpose – they weren't scratching itchy ears or butts, for example. Instead, the team hypothesizes that it might serve a social purpose.
"By copying someone else's behavior, you show that you notice and maybe even like that individual. So, it might help strengthen social bonds and create a sense of belonging within the group, just like it does in humans,"
says
Edwin van Leeuwen, biologist at Utrecht University in the Netherlands.
A chimp showing off its trendy new ear grass. (Jake Brooker/Chimfunshi Wildlife Orphanage Trust)
Intriguingly, the event wasn't the first time Chimfunshi chimps had decorated their orifices with grass. An original trendsetter named Julie started the whole grass-in-ear thing way back in 2010, which caught on with seven other chimps. The behavior continues to this day among the group, even after Julie's death.
This seems to be a case of
social learning
and
cultural transmission
– after all, only one of the four groups observed back then exhibited the behavior, even though all lived in similar conditions. Weirdest of all is that more than a decade after Julie, Juma seems to have come up with the idea independently, since his group never had contact with hers.
The researchers suggest that fads with no clear purpose could be a holdover from the important ability to learn new
survival skills
. It's telling that wild chimps haven't been observed following 'useless' trends – only captive ones seem to have enough time on their hands.
"Chimpanzees can socially learn novel skills and primarily use them in contexts of personal interest, like nut-cracking and termite fishing," the researchers
write in a paper
about their observations.
"Yet, when selection pressures relax (e.g., due to systematic provisioning in captive care), chimpanzees may extend their social learning occasionally to behaviors without direct instrumental utility."
Non-functional
cultural trends
aren't unique to chimps either. In recent years, orcas have been seen
wearing dead salmon
on their heads like hats, and
sinking boats
in European waters – both of which seem to be fads.
A group of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (
Tursiops aduncus
) in South Australia started '
tail-walking
' along the surface of the water after one of them observed captive dolphins that had been trained to do the trick. Wild dolphins continued to perform the feat for decades afterwards, indicating the trend had been passed down culturally.
Studying animal cultures could help teach us more about our own. After all, is sticking grass in your butt really that different from
planking
or
eating laundry detergent pods
?
The research was published in the journal
Behaviour
.

data.title: A job queue in two lines of JavaScript
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了如何用两行JavaScript代码实现一个任务队列，确保任务按顺序执行。代码定义了一个`Job`类型和`enqueue`函数，利用Promise链处理任务的顺序，即使链中出现错误，任务依然会被执行。文章还提到，简单的`chain.then(job)`可能导致任务在链出错时不执行，因此建议使用`chain.then(job, job)`。此外，文章包含其他技术话题的简要提及和作者的一些个人观点与经历。文章末尾有作者的招聘广告和版权声明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用链式Promise实现任务队列的可行性及其实现细节的讨论

不同观点：
• lerp-io认为，通过在enqueue()中不断创建新的Promise并引用前一个Promise，会导致Promise链不断增长，从而产生垃圾回收（GC）压力，因为这些Promise无法被垃圾回收。
• egorfine指出，这种实现方式并不是JavaScript（JS）中的常见做法，并给出了一个Job类型定义，暗示应使用更标准的JS方法。
• Inviz认为，链式Promise在处理高吞吐量场景时并不合适，因为会产生GC压力，但在普通场景下是可行的。
• theThree提供了一个使用async/await处理任务的示例代码，展示了如何顺序执行任务并捕获异常。
• cluckindan补充，如果在任务失败时需要记录日志，需要在Promise链中添加.catch()来处理错误，否则日志记录需要在任务本身中完成。
• vivzkestrel认为，生产级别的应用需要更健壮的机制，例如使用BullMQ这样的库来实现任务队列。
• neals表示对代码不理解，寻求详细的解释。
• 90s_dev分享了自己的类似经历，提到曾用类似的技巧处理一个Chrome特有的API的竞态条件，但最终还是移除了该实现。
• gabrielsroka指出，theThree提供的代码示例是TypeScript（TS）而不是JS。

补充讨论：
• 关于链式Promise是否适用于高吞吐量场景存在争议。lerp-io和Inviz都提到了GC压力问题，但Inviz认为在普通场景下是可行的。
• 讨论中涉及到对任务队列的不同实现方式，包括基础的Promise链和更高级的库如BullMQ。
• 对代码示例的语言类型存在误解，gabrielsroka指出了theThree的代码是TS而非JS。
• 90s_dev的经验分享提供了一个实际使用中的案例，尽管最终该实现被移除，但为讨论增加了一个实际场景的视角。

• 观点二：评论者可能对“safe word”的概念不熟悉，误解了其功能，将其当作一种推进活动的信号，而不是停止活动的信号。

data.title: Bypassing Google's big anti-adblock update
data.author: deryilz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何发现Google Chrome在MV3更新中绕过广告拦截限制的漏洞。MV3更新取消了`webRequestBlocking`权限，导致广告拦截器无法正常工作。作者发现，尽管`chrome.webRequest` API在MV3中不再支持`blocking`功能，但由于JavaScript绑定实现的漏洞，可以通过伪造事件并利用`opt_webViewInstanceId`参数绕过权限检查，从而恢复广告拦截功能。该漏洞的根本原因在于Chrome对JavaScript绑定的处理不当，使得扩展程序能够绕过安全验证。作者在2023年报告了此漏洞，并认为这是他遇到的最有趣的漏洞之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google的MV3政策及其对广告拦截器和浏览器选择的影响

不同观点：
• al_borland认为，反对Google举措的唯一正确做法是放弃使用Chrome及所有基于Chromium的浏览器，以削弱Google对网络未来方向的垄断。
• breve推荐使用Firefox，因为uBlock Origin在Firefox上表现最佳，并提供了相关链接支持其观点。
• krackers质疑Google对MV3安全性的声明，指出MV3并不比MV2更安全。
• jacquesm将广告拦截器比喻为“大脑的防火墙”，批评Google在广告内容控制上的垄断地位，尤其对YouTube的广告策略表示不满。
• throwaway73945认为OP让Google修补了一个无害的“问题”，而这个问题本可以被插件开发者用来绕过MV3的限制。
• crazygringo反驳关于webRequestBlocking的普遍观点，声称uBlock Origin Lite与Chrome和MV3配合良好，并指出新版本在性能上的改进。
• raydenvm建议使用Brave浏览器，并提供相关文章链接，说明Brave对MV3的应对措施。
• zulban主张使用Firefox和Linux来避免被Google和Windows的商业模式影响，质疑“绕过”策略的长期有效性。

• urda简单直接地建议通过安装Firefox来绕过Chrome的问题。

• RockstarSprain对Firefox表示了一定的兴趣，但指出其无法安装PWAs的问题，并提到一个第三方扩展，但对其隐私安全性有所担忧。
• loloquwowndueo表示在工作笔记本上不得不使用Chrome，但在其他设备上使用Firefox，并对uBlock Origin在工作中的作用表示赞赏。
• daft_pink询问是否可以通过使用其他基于Chrome的浏览器来避免MV3的影响，并寻求隐私保护的建议。

补充讨论：
1. 关于浏览器选择的讨论主要集中在Chrome、Firefox和Brave之间，用户对隐私、性能和广告拦截功能有不同偏好。
2. MV3政策对广告拦截器的影响是争议的焦点，尤其是它对用户体验和开发者社区的影响。
3. 讨论中多次提到使用非Chrome浏览器（如Firefox和Brave）作为绕过Google政策的方法，并提供了具体的技术建议和链接。
4. 对广告内容的控制和Google的垄断地位是用户不满的主要来源，尤其是对YouTube广告的不满。
5. 用户对不同浏览器的PWA支持和隐私保护功能表现出关注，尤其是Firefox在这方面的不足被提及。

44544266.article_content:
D
erin Eryılmaz
How I found a bypass in Google's big anti-adblock update
July 12, 2025
About MV3
If you know anything about browsers, you've probably heard that Google Chrome is phasing out MV2 in favor of MV3. You've probably also heard that this hurts adblockers.
A quick explainer: "MV" stands for "manifest version." MV3 introduces a new type of runtime for Chrome extensions that, among other things, gets rid of
webRequestBlocking
, a permission that allows extensions to block requests dynamically based on their content (which
its replacement
does not support). Adblockers heavily rely on
webRequestBlocking
to function properly. Pretty convenient (cough cough) for a company that makes most of its revenue from ads to be removing that.
Anyway, with the phasing-out of MV2 pretty much done, now seems like a good time to talk about a bug in Chrome that I found and reported to Google in 2023.
The bug
let
webRequestBlocking
(and yes, adblockers) work in MV3.
I still consider it probably the funniest bug I've ever found.
Stop writing browsers in JavaScript
Yes, Chrome is written in C++. However, extensions are written in JavaScript, and the API functions they call look just like JavaScript functions, at least from the extension's point of view. But they aren't normal functions: they're special and do browsery C++ stuff through bindings. In theory, this should be safe.
But in the old days, Google decided it'd be a good idea to inject a bunch of JS files into pages that used Chrome APIs. These "extension binding modules" would initialize API functions and validate arguments before passing them to the browser.
(Note:
here's the codebase
of those files in 2016.)
Turns out running privileged JavaScript in user-controlled websites was not a good idea, because JS can often be manipulated by overriding global functions and prototypes. Since certain APIs like
chrome.runtime
exist on normal websites too, the extension bindings system led to multiple Universal XSS bugs back in 2015 and 2016.
Here's one
that allows any website to inject code into any other website. Truly crazy stuff. If only I weren't 8 years old back then... maybe I could have cashed in.
Anyway, Google learned from their mistake and moved most API bindings to pure C++. However, a couple of JS binding files still exist and are used today. For example, if a Chrome extension runs the following code, it'll hit a
JS loop
and hang infinitely: (as of July 2025)
chrome.permissions.contains({ permissions: { length: Infinity }})
Maybe you are wondering what this has to do with adblockers.
Remember how I said only a few APIs still use JavaScript bindings?
chrome.webRequest
is one of them.
The bug
This is how an MV2 extension would block requests to example.com:
chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.addListener(() => {
return { cancel: true }
}, { urls: ['*://*.example.com/*'] }, ['blocking'])
It's the
'blocking'
part at the end that requires the
webRequestBlocking
permission, and therefore isn't allowed in MV3. Without it, the
cancel: true
does nothing.
So clearly adding a blocking listener to the
chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest
event does not work anymore. But we can do something crazy. We can make
our own event.
Now, this should not be possible; it's not even a concept that makes sense. But, because of how the JS bindings work, you can do it. For some reason, there is a
wrapper class
for
webRequest
events that contains some extra state.
(A
note on the security
of the above code.)
Instead of doing pure bindings between JS and C++, the browser creates one of these classes for every
chrome.webRequest
event:
onBeforeRequest
,
onCompleted
, etc. Surprisingly, the
.constructor
of these events is still public. It points to yet another wrapper class, which internally calls
WebRequestEventImpl
(from the code above). You can use this to can create a new event with your own properties:
let WebRequestEvent = chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.constructor
let fooEvent = new WebRequestEvent("foo")
There is still a lot of validation going on in the backend when you try to actually do things with these fake events. For example, trying to add a listener to
fooEvent
kills the extension's process, because the event name is invalid. So how do you manipulate the properties of
WebRequestEventImpl
to do anything interesting?
After a lot of time looking into the C++ code, I found exactly one vulnerable thing: the
opt_webViewInstanceId
parameter. This was set for Chrome platform apps, in order to let them manage their embedded websites (WebViews). Among other things, it let them use web request blocking to control navigation. Basically, if an event had a WebView ID, the permission check for
webRequestBlocking
would be skipped
. The issue was that the browser never verified that an event with a WebView ID actually belonged to a platform app. So an extension could spoof it, skip the check, and use the blocking feature.
let WebRequestEvent = chrome.webRequest.onBeforeRequest.constructor
// opt_web

data.title: What Happened to All the Human Bird Flu Cases?
data.author: Gaishan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了美国自特朗普政府以来对H5N1禽流感的应对，特别是在没有报告人类感染病例后，疾控中心宣布结束紧急响应，改为每月更新。尽管2024年底感染病例在美国多州增加，但自今年2月以来，未报告新病例，总数保持在70例。文章指出，感染减少的原因令人困惑，可能与野生鸟类迁徙及监测人员削减有关，但也反映出对禽流感理解的不足。特别是在移民劳工等脆弱群体中，由于担心移民身份问题，许多人不愿接受检测，导致潜在感染未被发现。文章强调，目前的监测系统主要围绕暴露且有症状者，无法全面覆盖，感染可能被严重低估。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对监控机制是否有效存在的不同看法

不同观点：
• LarsDu88认为，监控机制已经被拆除，依赖于移民劳工的农民群体被迫保持沉默。他担心可能已经出现了疫情爆发，但外界无法得知。这表明他对当前的监控和透明度非常不信任，尤其在涉及弱势群体时。

• blackqueeriroh则持相反观点，认为加州仍然保持了强有力的监控机制，暗示LarsDu88的担忧并不成立，至少在加州，疫情监控仍在有效运作。

• tiahura没有明确表达观点，而是通过提供CDC（美国疾病控制与预防中心）的链接，暗示读者可以参考官方资源来获取有关疫情监控的信息。这可以被视为一种中立的、基于数据的视角。

补充讨论：
• LarsDu88的评论中提到了移民劳工被迫沉默的情况，这可能暗示了社会不公和对某些群体的忽视，这是讨论中的一个潜在问题。

• 争议的焦点在于监控机制的有效性以及信息透明度。LarsDu88认为监控缺失，可能导致疫情信息被掩盖，而blackqueeriroh则认为监控仍然有效，争议的核心是对于政府和公共卫生机构的信任问题。

• tiahura提供的链接指向了一个具体的监控系统（国家野生动物健康监测系统），虽然这个系统主要关注野生动物健康，但它表明了在疫情监控中多层次和多部门合作的重要性。

F
rom the outset
of the Trump administration, bird flu, or H5N1 avian influenza, has flown rather conspicuously — and in fact quite mysteriously — under the radar. So much so that this week, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
announced
the end of its emergency response to bird flu, citing the lack of reported human cases. Updates, previously issued weekly, will now arrive
monthly
. But something isn’t adding up.
Related
The Looming Threat of H5N1
At the end of 2024, infections in the United States were surging. From Ohio to California, and in a swath of intervening states, diagnoses were being made in growing numbers of farmworkers who came into contact with infected
cattle
and poultry. Most
suffered
a mild spectrum of symptoms — low grade fevers, muscle aches, inflammation in their eyes. As cases swelled, an older man in Louisiana fell critically ill. He would eventually become the first person in the U.S. to
succumb
to the virus since initial human cases were reported to the World Health Organization in 1997. data.title: OpenAI’s Windsurf deal is off, and Windsurf’s CEO is going to Google
data.author: rcchen
data.article_summary: OpenAI收购AI编程初创公司Windsurf的交易告吹。相反，Windsurf的CEO Varun Mohan及其联合创始人Douglas Chen，以及部分研发团队将加入Google DeepMind，专注于Gemini等项目。Windsurf的业务主管Jeff Wang成为临时CEO，全球销售副总裁Graham Moreno升任总裁。Google获得了Windsurf部分技术的非独占许可，但不会拥有Windsurf的股份。此前，OpenAI曾计划以30亿美元收购Windsurf。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windsurf和Cursor等AI代码编辑器公司的收购、估值和员工待遇问题。

不同观点：
• **对收购和估值的质疑**：
  - [hedayet] 质疑Windsurf和Cursor等公司的高估值，认为它们缺乏专有技术或模型来支撑数十亿美元的估值。
  - [rvnx] 认为Windsurf和Cursor只是ChatGPT和Claude的转售商，技术本身并不值得高估值。
  - [asdev] 提到类似情况，如WIX以8000万美元收购Lovable.dev的 clone，认为当前AI收购泡沫严重。

• **对员工待遇的不满**：
  - [metadat] 提到普通员工在收购中未获得应有回报，创始人或研究人员则受益，认为这对普通员工不公平。
  - [nrmitchi] 和[screye] 都提到这种“假收购”对普通员工不公，员工未得到应有补偿，呼吁应立法和监管。
  - [dalemhurley] 指出VC资金推动公司快速增长，但员工未必能从中受益。

• **技术趋势和工具选择**：
  - [submeta] 认为CLI工具（如Claude Code）比传统IDE（如VS Code、Cursor）更高效，软件开发的现实正在改变，开发者应更多关注设计、规划和测试，而非文件导航和修改。
  - [extr] 支持CLI工具的优越性，认为IDE的开发和维护成本高昂，而CLI工具提供了足够的功能且更具成本效益。

• **对收购背后动机的分析**：
  - [Ancalagon] 认为Google、Meta等大公司通过挖走AI初创公司的顶尖人才来削弱这些公司，而不是直接收购，可能是为了规避垄断诉讼。
  - [neilv] 质疑Google为何选择不直接收购Windsurf，而是通过获取人才和技术授权的方式，认为这种做法可能对初创公司及其投资者不利。

补充讨论：
• **市场竞争和创新压力**：
  - [dalemhurley] 指出Cursor和GitHub Copilot等工具面临开源社区的激烈竞争，认为它们的市场护城河很浅，必须不断创新以维持增长。
  - [diegof79] 以用户体验角度指出Windsurf在产品更新中出现问题，导致用户流失，可能影响了OpenAI对收购的兴趣。

• **对行业动向的预测**：
  - [wagwang] 认为AI行业的快速变化和估值泡沫破裂将带来一个值得记录的行业故事。
  - [3abiton] 提到当前OpenAI的戏剧性事件，猜测是Google挖走了Windsurf的人才还是OpenAI取消了交易，并预测亚马逊/微软将是下一个动作方。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在AI初创公司的高估值是否合理、普通员工在收购中未得到公平对待以及大公司通过挖角而非收购来削弱初创公司的做法是否道德。

AI

OpenAI’s Windsurf deal is off — and Windsurf’s CEO is going to Google
Key researchers from the AI coding startup are also heading to Google.
Key researchers from the AI coding startup are also heading to Google.
by
Hayden Field
Jul 11, 2025, 9:22 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Photo: Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images
Hayden Field
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
OpenAI’s deal to buy Windsurf is off, and Google will instead hire Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, cofounder Douglas Chen, and some of Windsurf’s R&D employees and bring them onto the Google DeepMind team, Google and Windsurf announced Friday.
Mohan and the Windsurf employees will focus on agentic coding efforts at Google DeepMind and work largely on Gemini. Google will not have any control over nor a stake in Windsurf, but it will take a non-exclusive license to some of Windsurf’s technology.
Effective immediately, Jeff Wang, Windsurf’s head of business, has become interim CEO, and Graham Moreno, its VP of global sales, will be Windsurf’s new president.
“Gemini is one of the best models available and we’ve been investing in its advanced capabilities for developers,” Chris Pappas, a spokesperson for Google, told
The Verge
in a statement. “We’re excited to welcome some top AI coding talent from Windsurf’s team to Google DeepMind to advance our work in agentic coding.”
“We are excited to be joining Google DeepMind along with some of the Windsurf team,” Mohan and Chen said in a statement. “We are proud of what Windsurf has built over the last four years and are excited to see it move forward with their world class team and kick-start the next phase.”
Google didn’t share how much it was paying to bring on the team. OpenAI was previously reported to be buying Windsurf for $3 billion.

data.title: A.I. Is Making Sure You Pay for That Ding on Your Rental Car
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hertz租车公司在车辆归还后通过AI扫描系统收取损害费用的合理性及消费者应对策略

不同观点：
• **质疑系统公正性与收费透明度**：
   - remram指出，如果在还车时没有当场检查并指出问题，事后收到账单令人难以接受。这种事后收费的做法让人质疑如何在争议中维权。
   - nitwit005通过引用实例，指出Hertz不仅收取损害费用，还附加各种处理费用，认为这是明显的骗局。

• **支持AI扫描系统，认为现状有改进**：
   - legitster认为当前的人工检查流程同样存在不公平，而AI扫描系统至少是透明和公正的。他并不认为Hertz有特别恶劣的行为。
   - benced则表示，随着时间的推移，这种做法会趋于合理化，因为租车行业竞争激烈，初期的问题会逐渐解决。

• **认为公司通过保险和费用牟利**：
   - pseudolus和kjellsbells认为Hertz通过促使顾客购买高额保险（如碰撞损害豁免）来增加收入，并且可能通过降低车辆价值和收取高额费用来持续压榨顾客。
   - kevingadd提到自己因类似问题选择购买损害保险，虽然增加了租车成本，但避免了不必要的麻烦。

• **个人经历与经验分享**：
   - zippyman55分享了自己在租车时遇到轮胎损坏的问题，并通过 escalation 解决了问题，提醒大家在租车时仔细检查车辆状况。
   - boznz建议在国外租车时查看旅行保险，因为这可能涵盖超额费用，并提到自己会在租车前后用手机拍照记录车况。
   - t1234s强调了购买损失损害豁免的重要性，因为普通保险可能不涵盖租车公司的停运损失。

• **对Hertz的全面抵制与批评**：
   - alwa和chris_wot直接建议不要与Hertz做生意，认为其品牌已失去信誉。
   - kevingadd引用了关于Hertz错误指控顾客的文章，表示自己因担心类似问题而选择其他租车公司。

• **幽默与讽刺**：
   - eggn00dles以幽默的方式表示，这可能是对人类反抗机器的测试，从中获取有价值的数据。
   - schrodinger则以讽刺的方式提出，如果在扫描区域外造成损害，公司将如何处理，暗示系统存在漏洞。

补充讨论：
- Hertz租车公司在损害检测和收费过程中是否公正透明是争议的焦点。
- 消费者如何通过保险和仔细检查车辆来保护自身利益是讨论中的重要策略。
- 对Hertz品牌形象的批评和不信任是普遍存在的主题。
- 讨论中也包含了一些对AI技术应用的幽默和讽刺，反映了对新技术的复杂态度。

data.title: ETH Zurich and EPFL to release a LLM developed on public infrastructure
data.author: andy99
data.article_summary: 2025年夏末，由EPFL、ETH Zurich和瑞士国家超级计算中心（CSCS）合作开发的完全开放的大语言模型（LLM）将发布。该模型在CSCS的“阿尔卑斯”超级计算机上训练，标志着开源AI和多语言能力的里程碑。模型具有超过1000种语言的 fluency，源代码和权重将公开，训练数据透明且可重现，旨在促进科学、社会和工业的创新与责任。该模型分为80亿和700亿参数两个版本，适用于广泛用户需求，并在遵守瑞士数据保护法和欧盟AI法案的前提下开发。这一项目得到了NVIDIA和HPE/Cray的长期合作支持，利用100%碳中和电力高效训练。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ETH和EPFL在开发大型语言模型（LLM）方面的努力、成就、挑战以及与全球其他模型的比较。

不同观点：
• isusmelj：认为ETH和EPFL正在基于旧的LLaMA模型进行训练或微调，性能可能不如最先进（SOTA）的模型。但重要的是这两所大学能够获得大规模训练的实践经验，尤其是在他们自己的基础设施上。强调基础设施在LLM中的关键作用。
• k__：对数据采集过程中尊重网络爬虫选择退出机制表示赞赏，认为这不会显著影响模型性能。
• defraudbah：对ETH Zurich的成就表示钦佩，认为该大学培养了大量优秀人才。
• hubraumhugo：作为瑞士人感到自豪，认为ETH和EPFL培养了世界级的创始人、研究人员和工程师，但瑞士常被美国遮掩。强调瑞士有机会在开放LLM领域创造 exceptional 的东西。
• bee_rider：认为数据集透明度是一个重要的进步，并开玩笑地建议将机器命名为AIps（AI Petaflops Supercomputer）。
• WeirderScience：强调开放训练数据的重要性，并好奇这种训练的可重复性。
• amelius：认为“AI民主化”正是这种开放性的体现。
• oytis：指出新闻稿更多地介绍了模型的开发过程，但很少提及与其他开放模型的性能比较。
• sschueller：提到瑞士被列入只能有限获取顶级AI芯片的第二梯队国家，链接了相关新闻。
• seydor：对多语言LLM与单语言模型的优劣表示好奇。
• kisamoto：希望了解上下文长度和其他技术细节，并对为何在未发布模型的情况下发布新闻稿表示疑问。
• wood_spirit：批评大公司开发的LLM存在广告、政治偏见等问题，认为欧洲学术界与政府合作有可能创造出更符合公共利益的AI。
• Tepix：询问该模型与Teuken和EuroLLM的比较。
• rkrisztian：对模型的8B参数表示失望，认为16GB VRAM的GPU上运行13B到16B的模型更为理想。
• Bengalilol：期待测试该模型。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是模型的性能与参数规模。rkrisztian认为8B参数的模型在常见GPU上不够理想，而isusmelj则认为性能可能不如SOTA模型。
• 另一个讨论点是数据集的开放性和透明度，WeirderScience和bee_rider对此表示赞赏，并认为这是一个重要的进步。
• 还有人关注瑞士在获取顶级AI芯片方面的限制，sschueller提供了相关链接并指出了这一问题。
• 对多语言LLM的优劣也存在疑问，seydor提出了这个问题但没有明确答案。
• 最后，关于新闻稿的发布时机和动机，kisamoto表示了疑问，认为在未发布模型的情况下发布新闻稿可能有其他动机。
